docs.title: Enterprise runtime model
docs.text:
Aspect Basic / Pro Enterprise Database local SQLite only PostgreSQL only Background processing integrated worker while the application is running independent FleetMiraWorker Windows service Workstations local Windows 10/11 console Windows 10/11 clients or Windows Server sessions Co-location application and SQLite on one workstation client, worker and PostgreSQL may share one server but remain independent components Central jobs processed in the application runtime queued in PostgreSQL and leased by one worker Backup SQLite diagnostic snapshot or manual complete ZIP64/directory set; Pro additionally provides configured archive backup PostgreSQL custom dump plus DDD, financial and record-document archives

Enterprise never falls back to SQLite. Client actions that need background processing create a central job; advisory locks, leases and idempotency keys prevent duplicate external effects when several workers are available.

docs.title: Highlights in 1.1.0-beta8
docs.text:
• time-based, mileage-based and combined fleet deadlines, including lead values, recurrence, odometer quality and personnel/fleet reports;
  • record documents for people and vehicles with drag-and-drop, versions, metadata, preview, independent retention, backup and audit;
  • target-independent Quick Backup for Basic/Pro database diagnostics or complete ZIP64/directory sets and Enterprise PostgreSQL diagnostics;
  • guided, verified relocation of the local data root in every edition;
  • complete record-level audit coverage for deadlines, documents, licence checks, tachograph links, odometer readings, costs, invoices, evidence and exports;
  • language-specific field guidance while region settings independently control date, time and number formatting;
  • conventional PC/SC RFID/NFC UID byte order for display, assignment and checks.

The Report dashboard guide describes twelve working-time, mileage, return and deadline reports. The Violation dashboard guide documents the risk screen, violation report and driver instruction using anonymised demo data.

docs.title: Data flows
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[FTP, DLT API or manual import] --> B[Hash and immutable local archive]
    B --> C{Content classification}
    C -->|C file| D[Driver-card parser and signature verification]
    C -->|M file| E[Vehicle-unit parser and signature verification]
    D --> F[Person, activities, deadlines and compliance]
    E --> G[Vehicle, activities, calibration and positions]
    B --> H[Verified cloud backup]
    I[(SQLite metadata and audit)] --> H

docs.title: Security and evidence
docs.text:
• Local passwords use Argon2id; accounts lock after repeated failed attempts.
  • Fixed roles are ADMIN, SUPPORT, OPERATOR and AUDITOR; services re-check permissions independently of the UI.
  • Secrets are DPAPI-protected on Windows and excluded from logs and audit.
  • Archived DDD files and cloud objects are hash-verified.
  • Logical deletion requires a reason. Audit entries cannot be edited through the application.
  • Database backups are produced through the SQLite backup API and pass integrity_check before upload.

docs.title: Supported languages and regions
docs.text: The application provides German, English and 21 additional European UI languages. Language and region are independent profile settings. English (en-GB) is the default for new deployments. Tachograph timestamps remain UTC regardless of region.

docs.title: Scope boundaries
docs.text: FLEET Mira provides technical controls and technical pre-checks. It does not replace legal assessment, employment-law decisions, national exception handling, a certified accounting system or the operator's procedural documentation.

docs.title: Detailed business guides
docs.text:
• Personnel and fleet tachodata evaluations
  • Driver-card analysis – every tab
  • Vehicle-unit analysis – every tab
  • Deadlines and record documents
  • Driving-licence checks and RFID/NFC
  • Vehicle costs and credits
  • Foreign invoices – workflow and every tab
  • Lease contracts, factor calculation and reports
  • E-invoice and XRechnung import
  • Cost analysis and reporting
  • Position maps for C and M data

These guides use a temporary anonymised copy of the development database. Activities, timestamps, amounts and approved coordinates remain representative. Driver names, dates of birth, card identities, registrations and VINs are replaced deterministically with recognisable demonstration values.

docs.title: Edition and processing model
docs.text: Basic and Pro use a local SQLite database and process background tasks in the application. Enterprise uses PostgreSQL exclusively. Its client places central work in the database queue; the independent FleetMiraWorker service performs imports, notifications, backup and other scheduled work. The same user workflow therefore produces the same business result, but Enterprise jobs may continue after the client window is closed.

docs.title: 1. Sign-in and workspace
docs.text:
Start FLEET Mira from the installed shortcut. The splash screen remains visible throughout startup initialization and the initial workspace load wave. Only after its UI callbacks have completed is the splash seamlessly replaced, within the same render cycle, by the immediately interactive sign-in dialog. A new installation uses admin / admin once and forces a secure replacement password. If an administrator has configured SSO and pre-assigned your account, select Sign in with Microsoft or Sign in with Google instead. Microsoft Entra ID SSO is currently beta and has not yet been validated end-to-end with a real customer tenant. Keep local sign-in available as a fallback until customer-specific acceptance is complete and contact your administrator if sign-in fails. Setup and troubleshooting are covered by the Administrator and integrator guide.

Figure: FLEET Mira splash screen before sign-in.

Figure: Local sign-in, Microsoft Entra SSO in untested beta status and regularly supported Google SSO.

After every sign-in, the Dashboard is the active page. The top navigation switches between the five main areas. Long operations show a non-modal loading status and may be cancelled; other tabs remain usable.

docs.title: User profile
docs.text:
Open User → My profile to change display name, email, language and region. Language or region changes take effect after the next sign-in. Table layouts, filters, splitter positions and column order are stored per user.

Editable fields, selection lists, date and number fields, and toggles provide concise input guidance. In forms, point to the field caption; for standalone filters or toggles, the guidance appears on the control itself. The description states the expected input, any applicable format or range, and the effect of the selection. It always follows the authenticated user's language, while date, time, and number formats continue to follow the selected region.

Figure: User-specific language, region and profile settings.

docs.title: Tables and context menus
docs.text:
• Click a header to sort; click again to reverse the direction.
  • Drag headers to change the column order and drag header boundaries to change widths.
  • Right-click a header to show or hide columns where offered.
  • Right-click a data row for object-specific actions. The row under the pointer is selected first.
  • Selected rows use a dark-blue background and white text, overriding status colours for readability.

docs.title: 2. Dashboard
docs.text:
The six photo-backed cards provide direct navigation:

Figure: Dashboard with anonymised demonstration data and direct navigation figures.

  • DLTNG devices: total, online and offline devices.
  • People/Vehicles: active master records.
  • Tachograph files: total C/M files, backup backlog/errors and latest imports.
  • Personnel deadlines / Vehicle deadlines: upcoming, due today and overdue items.
  • Driving-licence checks: pending clarification, checks due soon, overdue checks and the latest successful check.

Click an individual figure, not only the card, to open the corresponding pre-filtered list. Select Refresh dashboard after major imports when an immediate refresh is needed.

Basic always shows these six widgets in the fixed default layout. In Pro and Enterprise, Configure dashboard 💎 opens a personal editing mode on a 6×4 grid. Use the catalogue to show or hide widgets and drag them by their handle. A free area accepts the widget; dropping it on one equally sized widget swaps their positions. Save stores the layout for the signed-in user across workstations, Cancel discards the draft, and Restore default restores all six 2×2 widgets before saving.

Figure: Editing mode with the 6×4 grid, widget catalogue and drag handles.

docs.title: 3. Device Management
docs.text:
Figure: Device list and device-management workspace.

The device list can be filtered by name, tenant, site, group and status. Depending on permission, the toolbar and context menu allow you to:

  1. create, edit or duplicate a device;
  2. check status for one device or the current result set;
  3. open the embedded or standard browser interface;
  4. retrieve system information, remote files and the website log;
  5. deactivate or archive a device with confirmation.

The lower detail pages show master data, files, status history and audit. Remote file downloads use the configured destination and never alter the archive until the normal import path processes them.

docs.title: 4. Sources and download tasks
docs.text:
Open Administration → Sources to configure FTP, DLT API and SFTP endpoints, local folders, or UNC server shares. Test the connection before assigning a source to a task. Credentials and SFTP key passphrases are protected and do not appear in logs.

Figure: Administration of automatic import sources.

Open Administration → Tasks to define source selection, file patterns, recursion, schedule, archive behaviour and optional strict cloud-backup mode. Run now opens a detailed progress view with one row per source and live log messages. View latest log in the context menu opens the most recently stored execution with its trigger, run status, counters, source details and file details; unfinished runs remain visible. RFID terminal CSV files require RFID_*.CSV in the pattern.

The Administration → Settings → Automatically import USB removable drives option recursively scans newly inserted drives for DDD and RFID*.CSV files. It operates only while FLEET Mira is open or running in the system tray; source files remain on the drive.

docs.title: Data root and storage paths
docs.text: Under Administration → Settings, administrators can see the active data root and the fully resolved log, SQLite, DDD archive, document archive and financial archive paths. These fields remain read-only so files, database references and access permissions cannot be separated. Relocate data root … opens a guided wizard that copies and verifies the complete local root, normalises internal paths and restarts FLEET Mira through the new machine-wide locator. The target must be empty and on a fixed local drive. Enterprise moves only its local application root; PostgreSQL and deliberately external archives remain in place.

docs.title: Quick Backup and central backup jobs
docs.text:
Under Administration → Backups → Quick Backup, Basic and Pro choose between Database only and Complete manual backup. The database option remains a consistent, read-back-verified diagnostic ZIP. The complete backup also contains active DDD, financial and record-document archives with their manifests and can be written as either a portable ZIP64 file or a backup directory on a local or UNC destination. Optionally encrypted sets require a separately exported recovery key. The restore wizard supports both formats.

In Enterprise, Quick Backup requests the dedicated backup credentials and creates a PostgreSQL custom dump through the worker. Complete Enterprise backup jobs additionally process the configured DDD, financial and record-document archives. Closing the Enterprise client does not cancel a job already accepted by FleetMiraWorker.

Figure: Backup configuration, verification state and manual actions.

Figure: Scheduled and manually executable download tasks.

In strict mode, a terminal file is not marked as processed or deleted until its cloud copy is verified.

docs.title: 5. Tachodata Archive
docs.text:
Figure: Filterable C/M tachodata archive with status columns.

The archive contains driver-card C files and vehicle-unit M files. Filter by date, name, driver/vehicle, file type, generation, parser status, signature status, deletion state or backup state.

docs.title: Import and status
docs.text:
• Import DDD files accepts one or more local files.
  • Content determines C/M type; the filename is only a hint.
  • Successful parsing stores structured details without changing the original archive object.
  • VALID means all available signatures and the chain could be verified.
  • INVALID or UNVERIFIABLE places the file in quarantine; it remains viewable and exportable but cannot drive trusted links or combined evaluations.

docs.title: Open, export and delete
docs.text:
• Double-click or choose Open analysis to open the C or M analysis.
  • One selected row exports the original DDD; several rows or the current view export a ZIP.
  • Logical deletion requires a reason and is recorded in audit. It does not automatically delete a verified cloud backup.
  • Details / Signature / Audit explains hashes, parser warnings, signature sections and history.

docs.title: Backup status
docs.text: Verified is shown only after complete upload and remote hash verification. Use the context menu to retry, verify or restore a file. Backup errors are also linked from the dashboard.

docs.title: 6. Driver-card analysis
docs.text:
The header identifies the driver, card number and selected archive file. The analysis always uses the selected C file as its base.

Figure: Driver-card analysis for one selected C archive.

Tab Purpose Overview identity, validity, issuing authorities, generation and data range Activities sortable activity intervals in the configured time basis with C/M availability Day / Week graphical timelines, totals and details for the selected period DDD week view Web browser-style interactive week view using the selected file Events / Faults technical records from the card Vehicles used vehicle identifiers observed on the card Positions location list and interactive map Violations technical EU 561/2006 pre-check Signatures chain and per-EF verification results

The Data availability filter distinguishes all activities, C and M available, driver card only and vehicle unit only. The other source is comparison evidence; it never replaces the selected base file. Tachograph source data remains stored unchanged in UTC. Display and calculations use UTC by default. When Use local time for activities and calculations is enabled under System → Settings, display, day/week boundaries and compliance evaluations instead use the selected time zone. Daylight-saving transitions change neither source values nor elapsed durations.

docs.title: 7. Vehicle-unit analysis
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle-unit analysis for one selected M archive.

The M analysis shows vehicle identity and the selected M file. Driver sessions are grouped by normalised card number and generation. Team driving displays slot 1 and slot 2 separately.

Tabs include drivers, activities, day/week timelines, events/faults, speed, technical data, calibrations, positions/borders/loading, signatures and violations. Technical data uses a field tree; Calibrations lists calibration time, next calibration, workshop, VIN and registration. Position tabs can open the interactive map.

“No assigned driver card” means the M file contains slot activity for which no active card-insertion interval with a usable card number was found. It does not mean that a matching C archive is merely missing; the tooltip in day/week views explains this distinction.

docs.title: 8. Fleet Management
docs.text:
The compact left icon navigation opens non-duplicated work tabs and behaves the same in Fleet Management and Administration. A + or − to the left of a parent item expands or collapses its children. The context menu shows fixed pairs for Expand/Collapse item, Expand/Collapse group, and Expand/Collapse all; actions that do not apply are disabled. Group recursively affects the complete top-level subtree, including nested areas such as Traffic offences and External invoices. The state is stored for the signed-in user. Users without a stored preference start with the navigation fully collapsed. A new session starts with an empty workspace in both areas.

In Administration, Operations, Users and security, Communication and integrations, and Finance and system are the parent groups. Their pages are child entries and each opens one closable, movable work tab on the right. Selecting an already open child focuses its tab instead of creating a duplicate.

Figure: Fleet Management icon navigation and non-duplicated work tabs.

docs.title: Master data
docs.text:
• People: personal number, identity, contact data, licence data, FSK policy and status.
  • Vehicles: internal number, registration, VIN, type and status.
  • Due types: system and user-defined deadline categories for people or vehicles.
  • Suppliers / Cost categories: finance master data.

Figure: Personnel master-data list.

Figure: Vehicle master-data list.

Double-click a person or vehicle to open its record. Context menus jump directly to deadlines, tachodata, RFID or finance pages.

Use Fleet > Cost analysis to evaluate booked vehicle costs. Its initial period runs from the start of the current year through today; administrators can change the global default under Administration > Cost analysis > Calculation parameters.

docs.title: Person record
docs.text:
Figure: Person record with related business tabs.

The record contains master data, deadlines, documents, licence checks, RFID history, card links/files, day/week/activity views and audit. The Audit tab uses the same context menu as the global Audit Log: open the related record, show the XML tree view, or copy details, rows and cells. The Documents tab accepts drag-and-drop or file selection, versioning and metadata; PDF and image files can be previewed directly. Document and validity dates use date pickers formatted for the signed-in user's region. The immutable local original is created when the document is added, while the configured backup task handles external backup. Logical archiving remains available from the context menu. Local restore and permanent purge are visible only to appropriately authorised administrators. Use Assign RFID/NFC to read a UID from a local PC/SC reader. FSK via PC/SC records a successful check only when the read UID belongs to the selected person.

For a new record document, the document date defaults to today. Valid until is calculated from the document date plus the period configured under Administration → Receipts/Documents → Document retention period. The financial-document retention period remains independent.

The Audit tab covers the complete record. In addition to personnel or vehicle master-data changes, it includes logged events for related deadlines, documents, driving-licence checks and tachograph links. Vehicle records additionally include odometer readings, costs/credits, associated supplier invoices, financial documents and accounting exports. The Area column identifies the related sub-object.

docs.title: Vehicle record
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle record with tachograph, finance and position tabs.

The Master data tab opens the existing modal vehicle form through Edit vehicle. It also shows the latest reliable odometer reading with its source and quality, and the last known human-readable location. With an active telematics assignment, Open telematics opens a dedicated workspace for current location, route history, combined positions and events.

The Positions tab globally merges tachograph and telematics evidence, clearly labels its source and provides a source filter. Only telematics points form the route line in Route history; tachograph positions can be shown as reference markers.

Tabs include deadlines, documents, costs/credits, foreign invoices, lease, positions and audit. Tachograph links, mass-memory files, day/week views, infringements, drivers/activities, events/faults, speeds, technical data and calibrations are grouped below Tachodata. The Audit tab uses the same context menu as the global Audit Log: open the related record, show the XML tree view, or copy details, rows and cells. Record documents use the same audit-oriented archive and configured local, UNC or cloud backup destination. Aggregate functional tables hide the source-file column by default; the source archive remains available from the context menu. Identical technical records appear once with their source count and complete detail tree. Position rows can be opened together on the map.

docs.title: Odometer determination
docs.text:
FLEET Mira uses the same central odometer resolver for mileage reports and cost per kilometre. Manage the system-wide calculation rules under Administration → Cost analysis → Calculation parameters → Odometer determination. The provider tab Administration → Telematics → GPS-server.net additionally controls retention of telematics daily readings; use Mileage rules there to enable an override for an individual linked vehicle.

The settings shown in the standard dialog have the following meaning:

Setting Default Meaning Position detail retention (days) 28 Position points and sensor parameters are purged after 28 days. Qualified daily odometer readings are retained separately. Retain daily odometer readings (years) 6 Consolidated telematics daily readings are retained for six years. The permitted range is 1 to 20 years; Unlimited disables this purge. Missing period boundaries Extrapolate If a day or month has no sufficiently recent actual reading at its boundary, the following rules estimate it. This also applies to the current day once it has started. The alternatives are Interpolate and Incomplete. Estimation basis (days) 14 Depending on direction, extrapolation considers up to 14 plausible daily distances before or after the missing boundary. Minimum daily values 3 At least three usable daily distances are required for extrapolation. Maximum estimation gap (days) 7 The gap between the actual support reading and the missing boundary must not exceed seven days. For interpolation, this limit applies on both sides.

FLEET Mira first searches the 24 hours before the period boundary for a qualified actual reading. If several sources are available, the following priority is mandatory:

  1. M-file midnight reading (M_MIDNIGHT)
  2. Telematics sensor (GPS_SERVER_SENSOR)
  3. C-file vehicle use (C_VEHICLE_USE)
  4. C-file place (C_PLACE)
  5. C-file three-hour GNSS position (C_GNSS_3H)
  6. Telematics GPS (GPS_SERVER_GPS)

Only readings with quality Valid or Warning are eligible. Unverified, unknown, manual or conflicting readings are excluded. The newest reading wins within the same source. A higher-priority reading can therefore override a slightly newer lower-priority reading as long as it is not older than 24 hours.

Source-priority example: At the 1 July 00:00 boundary, an M-file midnight reading of 80,000 km was measured at 23:58 and a telematics sensor reading of 80,005 km at 23:59. Both are recent and qualified, so the M-file value of 80,000 km is used. If the M-file value is absent, the sensor value is used.

With Interpolate, the resolver draws a straight line between the latest qualified reading before the boundary and the first qualified reading after it. Both support readings must lie within the maximum estimation gap, must be compatible and must not produce an odometer rollback:

Estimated value = previous reading + elapsed share × (following reading − previous reading)

Interpolation example: A reading of 120,000 km is available for 10 July 00:00 and 120,800 km for 14 July 00:00. Two of the four days have elapsed at the 12 July boundary. The interpolated reading is 120,000 + 2/4 × 800 = 120,400 km.

With Extrapolate, FLEET Mira calculates the median of the plausible daily distances in the estimation basis. A missing closing boundary is projected forwards from the latest actual reading. If the opening boundary is missing and qualified readings only follow it, the same logic is applied symmetrically backwards from the first actual reading. Daily rates below 0 or above 1,800 km are rejected, and different GPS odometer kinds are not mixed:

Estimated value = latest actual reading + median daily distance × estimation gap

Opening reading = first following actual reading − median daily distance × estimation gap

Example using the default settings: The latest actual reading on 12 July is 120,000 km. The usable daily distances in the preceding 14 days are 180, 200 and 220 km, giving a median of 200 km. The gap to the 15 July boundary is three days. FLEET Mira calculates 120,000 + 200 × 3 = 120,600 km. With only two usable daily distances or an eight-day gap, the displayed settings would not permit an estimate and the boundary would remain incomplete.

Opening-boundary example: The first qualified reading after the start of the month is 80,200 km at 2 July 00:00. Three subsequent plausible daily distances have a median of 180 km. For the month boundary one day earlier, FLEET Mira derives an opening reading of 80,200 − 180 × 1 = 80,020 km.

Estimated values are not stored as actual odometer readings. The report exposes the result, method, support readings, measurement times, estimation distance and algorithm version. Opening and closing boundaries use the same configured strategy and quality limits. Both readings are rounded to whole kilometres first; the difference is then calculated exactly as closing − opening. For the current local day, FLEET Mira first uses the latest qualified actual reading from that day. If none exists and Extrapolate is configured, the reading is estimated up to the current calculation instant, not to the future midnight boundary. Daily, monthly and overall mileage and cost analysis share this central closing boundary. If no permitted estimate can be produced, an existing latest actual period reading remains usable as partial coverage. See Report dashboard for the detailed daily audit and Cost analysis and reporting for the identical use in cost per kilometre.

docs.title: 9. Deadlines and download due dates
docs.text:
Personnel and vehicle deadline evaluations are separate but use the same sortable/filterable component. Personnel deadlines remain time-based. Vehicle deadlines can be time-based, mileage-based or combined; a combined deadline becomes due when the first limit is reached. Time and mileage lead values and recurrence intervals can be configured per deadline or as due-type defaults.

The fleet evaluation displays the latest reliable odometer reading, measurement time and source, target and remaining mileage, trigger and data quality. Filters cover due type, status, basis, trigger, mileage quality and evaluability. If a combined deadline has no valid mileage reading, its time condition remains usable while the mileage condition is marked only partially evaluable. Colours mean:

  • green: outside the lead time;
  • blue/orange status: approaching or due today;
  • red: overdue;
  • completed: closed with completion date.

Automatic download deadlines are managed by the system:

Figure: Filterable personnel deadline evaluation.

  • current driver card: readout date + 28 days;
  • vehicle unit matched by VIN: readout date + 90 days.

The readout date is taken from a valid C_YYYYMMDD_HHmm... or M_YYYYMMDD_HHmm... filename, then falls back to source creation, download and archive UTC dates. Automatic deadlines cannot be manually moved or completed. Tachograph calibration remains a separate vehicle deadline.

docs.title: 10. Driving-licence checks and RFID
docs.text:
The complete workflow for check policy, UID assignment, PC/SC checks, automatic follow-up dates, terminal CSV and exceptions is documented in Driving-licence checks and RFID/NFC. A system-managed deadline is completed only by a successful check; an unknown chip or a chip assigned to another person creates no success record.

The Personnel navigation provides:

Figure: Driving-licence-check (FSK) due-date evaluation.

  • FSK evaluation with interval, last check, next due date, terminal and status;
  • licence-check history;
  • RFID pending list for unknown UIDs or invalid CSV rows.

The default check interval is 28 days. Successful PC/SC, terminal CSV and resolved mobile records use the same service and update one managed FSK deadline. Assigning an RFID UID alone is not a check.

Unknown terminal UIDs remain pending. Assigning them creates the effective check; discarding requires a reason and never creates a permanent RFID assignment.

docs.title: 11. Notifications
docs.text:
Under Administration → Notifications, configure SMTP, responsible recipients, rules/templates and the send log. Recipients may be assigned to fleet management, system management or both; their To/CC type applies to both assignments. Double-clicking a recipient or rule opens its edit dialog. The system is disabled until SMTP and recipients have been tested and sending is explicitly enabled.

Figure: Notification rules, templates and schedules.

Standard rules cover weekly information, daily reminders from ten days, urgent reminders from three days, overdue warnings and a daily responsible-person report. Additional rules can distribute violation dashboards to managers and deliver each new driver instruction exactly once with its PDF attachment. Rules may be previewed or sent manually when the user has permission.

The Daily task status report system rule is sent exclusively to system managers at 07:00 each day by default. Immediately before delivery it checks every active DLTNG device and summarises scheduled and manual download tasks from the complete previous day. For each source it shows availability, error details and downloaded, successful, failed and skipped file counts. One UTF-8 CSV lists every successful or failed file; a report with a header-only CSV is also sent on days without a run. Previewing deliberately performs no live device access. Fleet status, cost analysis and violation dashboard reports remain exclusive to fleet managers.

docs.title: Direct vehicle costs
docs.text:
Open a vehicle record → Costs / Credits. Select category and type and enter document date, validity period, net and VAT. Variable allocates the full amount to the document date; fixed entries are distributed by day over their complete validity period. Amounts are stored to the cent. Draft, verification, booking, cancellation and credit are covered in Vehicle costs and credits.

Figure: Supplier master data for financial documents.

docs.title: Foreign invoices
docs.text:
Open Fleet → Foreign invoices. Double-click an invoice to open it as a work tab.

Figure: Foreign-invoice list and work-tab entry point.

flowchart LR
    A[Create draft header] --> B[Add vehicle positions]
    B --> C[Upload original documents]
    C --> D[Cloud hash verified]
    D --> E[Verify totals]
    E --> F[Book]
    F --> G[REST or CSV/ZIP accounting export]

The status row compares gross invoice amount, split amount and difference. Zero difference is green; any cent difference is red and blocks verification. Invoice-bound positions inherit the invoice date for document/valid-from/valid-to and are always variable. Booked data is immutable; corrections use cancellation or linked credits.

docs.title: Lease contracts
docs.text:
Use Fleet → Lease contracts to manage contract data, factor-based pre-calculation, the independently authoritative contract rate, payment schedule, documents and linked actual costs. Lease contracts explains the factor formulas, M-data mileage evidence and all three leasing reports.

Figure: Filterable lease-contract overview from the anonymised demo database.

docs.title: E-invoice/XRechnung
docs.text: Fleet → Import XRechnung guides users through KoSIT validation, invoice and supplier data, vehicle/category allocation, line splitting and totals reconciliation. Only confirmed creation atomically writes a foreign-invoice draft and locally verified original, XML and report objects. See E-invoice and XRechnung import.

docs.title: 13. Audit, reports and logs
docs.text:
The global audit under Administration → Audit combines device, tachograph and fleet events. Filter by date, user, action or text. Double-click an entry to open its current related object when the stable ID can be resolved. Structured JSON/XML details can be opened as a tree, exported as JSON and printed. Navigation itself is not audited.

Figure: Global audit log with object-based navigation.

Fleet → Violation dashboard 💎 provides period-based risk scoring, detailed findings, a dashboard report and tamper-evident driver instructions. Fleet → Report dashboard 💎 contains fifteen working-time, mileage, leasing, return and deadline reports with favourites, run history and PDF/Excel output. All screens, purpose descriptions and Stimulsoft PDF examples are shown in Violation dashboard and driver instructions and Report dashboard.

Deadline and evaluation grids support print preview, system printing and PDF. Only visible filtered rows and columns are included.

Administration → Logs shows app.log, REST logs and native crash diagnostics. Logs use English technical messages regardless of the selected UI language.

docs.title: 14. Tray and shutdown
docs.text: Closing the main window normally keeps background services running in the system tray. Use the tray action to restore the window. Use System → Exit application and services or the equivalent tray command for a clean shutdown; schedulers, REST API, notification service, backup coordinator and logs are closed in order.

docs.title: 15. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Action File is quarantined Open Details/Signatures; install missing crypto/trust material or verify the source. Do not re-label the file manually. Backup remains pending Test the active target, inspect quota/authentication and use Back up now. No PC/SC reader Install the reader driver, reconnect it and reopen the read dialog. No C/M comparison Verify matching card number, generation, UTC range and valid signature status. Invoice cannot be verified Resolve the split difference and ensure at least one original document is locally verified. Backup status does not block verification. UI job failed Use Retry, then inspect app.log with the displayed job/request ID.

For administrator-level recovery, continue with the Administrator and integrator guide.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: The accounting adapter transmits a booked foreign invoice, supplier, vehicle positions and original documents to a configured HTTPS endpoint. FLEET Mira is the HTTP client; the accounting system implements the receiver.

docs.title: 2. Preconditions
docs.text:
• invoice status is BOOKED;
  • header totals match active positions to the cent;
  • at least one original document is locally verified; backup status is irrelevant;
  • user has finance.export;
  • endpoint uses HTTPS;
  • no successful export exists for the same idempotency key.

docs.title: 3. Request
docs.text:
POST /configured/accounting/path HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...
Idempotency-Key: <stable-sha256>

Multipart fields:

Field Content type Meaning metadata application/json; charset=utf-8 complete versioned accounting bundle document_1...n original MIME type byte-identical, hash-verified originals

docs.title: 4. Metadata model
docs.text:
Top level:

Field Meaning format technical constant DLTNG-ACCOUNTING retained for compatibility version contract version invoice invoice header supplier supplier master snapshot positions vehicle-linked cost/credit positions

Important invoice fields include stable ID, document type/number/date, delivery date/number, cost centre, due date, payment/discount terms, net/tax/gross cents, status and currency. Supplier includes stable ID, supplier/creditor numbers, address, tax ID, phone and email. Positions include stable ID, vehicle ID/number/registration/VIN, category, type, description, validity/document dates, net/tax/gross cents, tax rate basis points and variable flag.

Amounts are integer cents. Tax rates are integer basis points (1900 = 19.00%). Credits are identified by type; stored amounts remain positive.

docs.title: 5. Idempotency
docs.text: The key is deterministic for invoice ID, booked revision and export contract version. A receiver must return the original successful result for a repeated key and must not post twice.

docs.title: 6. Response
docs.text:
Success (200 or 201):

{
  "status": "accepted",
  "external_id": "ACC-2026-004712",
  "message": "Imported"
}

external_id is persisted with response time. A non-2xx response keeps the outbox item retryable and stores a sanitised error. Authentication bodies/secrets are not audited.

docs.title: 7. Process
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant M as FLEET Mira
    participant V as Document vault
    participant A as Accounting endpoint
    U->>M: Transfer booked invoice
    M->>V: Download and hash-check originals
    M->>M: Build bundle and idempotency key
    M->>A: HTTPS multipart POST
    alt accepted
        A-->>M: external_id
        M->>M: Mark export successful and audit
    else temporary failure
        A-->>M: error
        M->>M: Persist outbox retry
    end

docs.title: 8. Receiver requirements
docs.text:
• enforce HTTPS and authenticated clients;
  • limit body size and accepted MIME types;
  • stream originals and verify declared hashes where exposed;
  • implement atomic invoice/document handling;
  • persist idempotency keys;
  • return stable external IDs;
  • redact credentials and document contents from logs.

docs.title: 9. Error handling
docs.text: Status Receiver meaning 400/422 permanent contract/validation error; operator correction required 401/403 credentials/permission error 409 idempotency or business conflict; return existing result when equivalent 413 payload exceeds receiver limit 429 retry later; honour Retry-After 5xx transient receiver failure; outbox retry

docs.title: 10. Compatibility
docs.text: Fields are additive within a contract version. Removing/renaming fields or changing amount semantics requires a new version. The legacy DLTNG-ACCOUNTING format token is deliberately not rebranded.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The DriverCard API exposes the same parsed driver-card data used by the FLEET Mira desktop analysis. It is intended for local integration and the bundled web week view. It does not modify archived originals.

Default base URL: http://127.0.0.1:5055. Start/stop/open/log commands are available under System. Binding beyond loopback requires an external TLS/authentication gateway and an explicit risk assessment.

docs.title: 2. Time, formats and filters
docs.text:
• timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC;
  • dates are YYYY-MM-DD;
  • durations are integer seconds unless stated otherwise;
  • card numbers are normalised strings;
  • JSON uses UTF-8;
  • validation errors return JSON with error and a readable message.

Common query parameters:

Parameter Meaning import_id parsed import identifier archive_id stable tachodata archive identifier card_number exact normalised card number date_from, date_to inclusive UTC date range limit, offset bounded pagination where supported

docs.title: 3. Endpoints
docs.text: Method and path Function GET /health process and database readiness POST /api/drivercard/parse parse a supplied DDD payload and persist/reuse its import GET /api/drivercard/imports list parsed driver-card imports GET /api/drivercard/time-summary activity totals by type GET /api/drivercard/activities activity intervals GET /api/drivercard/events card events GET /api/drivercard/faults card faults GET /api/drivercard/vehicles-used vehicles recorded on the card GET /api/drivercard/positions recorded positions GET /api/drivercard/day-overview prepared day data GET /api/drivercard/week-overview prepared ISO-week data GET /api/drivercard/eu561/violations technical EU 561/2006 pre-check

docs.title: 4. Health
docs.text:
GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:5055

{"status":"ok","service":"drivercard-rest","database":"available"}

docs.title: 5. Parse a driver card
docs.text:
POST /api/drivercard/parse accepts JSON. The desktop web preload uses base64 so no local archive path appears in the browser URL.

{
  "file_name": "C_20250715_0615_Demo_1000000000000001.DDD",
  "content_base64": "BASE64_DATA",
  "archive_id": "optional-stable-id"
}

The response identifies import/archive, driver/card metadata, activity range and parser warnings. Binary input, signatures and certificates are never echoed. A repeated identical payload is idempotent by hash.

docs.title: 6. Activities and summaries
docs.text:
GET /api/drivercard/activities?archive_id=ARCHIVE_ID&date_from=2025-07-14&date_to=2025-07-20

Activity rows contain start/end UTC, activity code (DRIVING, WORK, AVAILABILITY, REST), duration, card, crew and slot information. Day/week endpoints return the same source intervals grouped for visualisation; they are not separate evidence records.

docs.title: 7. Events, faults, vehicles and positions
docs.text: Event/fault responses include technical type/code, start/end and readable description where known. Unknown standard extensions remain represented by the technical code. Position rows contain timestamp, latitude, longitude, source/type, country/region codes and optional odometer.

docs.title: 8. EU 561/2006 pre-check
docs.text: The endpoint evaluates only the selected data basis. Its response includes driver summary, violations, warnings, rule/algorithm version and data-gap notices. It is a technical pre-check, not an authority/legal decision. National exceptions, AETR and Article 12 circumstances are not decided automatically.

docs.title: 9. HTTP status codes
docs.text: Status Meaning 200 successful query or idempotent parse 400 malformed payload/filter 404 archive/import not found 409 conflicting or quarantined data for the requested trusted operation 413 payload too large for configured limit 422 DDD content cannot be parsed 500 unexpected internal failure; correlate with REST log

docs.title: 10. Security and operation
docs.text:
• Keep loopback binding unless a protected integration gateway is deployed.
  • Do not put DDD data or local paths in query strings.
  • Restrict REST log access; logs are English and exclude raw DDD/secrets.
  • Stop the API through FLEET Mira before maintenance.
  • API paths and response field names retain their technical compatibility even though the visible product is FLEET Mira.

docs.title: Consistent administration UI
docs.text:
Administration pages use the shared structural contract from administration_ui.py. Business logic, permissions, and edition separation remain independent of this presentation contract. As in Fleet Management, an IconNavbar on the left shows functional groups as parent nodes and Administration pages as child nodes. A child opens one closable and movable work tab on the right. An already open page is focused instead of duplicated, and a new login starts with an empty workspace.

Functional group Administration pages Operations Sources, Tasks, Telematics, Backups Users and security Users, Single sign-on, Roles and permissions, Tachograph trust, Rule sets Communication and integrations Notifications, AI connector, Traffic offences Finance and system Cost analysis, Receipts/Documents, Settings, Audit log, Logs, Raw configuration

Administration and Fleet Management use the same recursive context-menu behavior. Expandable nodes show the fixed pairs Expand/Collapse item, Expand/Collapse group, and Expand/Collapse all. A leaf shows group and all; empty space only shows all. Actions that do not apply remain visible and disabled. Group actions always affect the complete subtree of the top-level parent. Expansion and splitter width are stored per user.

Group and page titles, tooltips, context menus, open work tabs, functional subtabs, and Pro badges are translated together into the authenticated user's language. English is used before authentication. Region changes only date, number, currency, and similar formatting, never navigation labels. The persisted navigation/admin page key remains compatible but does not automatically open a page at session start. Inaccessible pages remain visible as disabled children, explicitly licence-hidden pages remain hidden, and groups without an accessible page remain visible but disabled.

Each page is marked as list management, settings form, operational/status, read-only, or tab container. List pages show introduction, filters, action bar, data grid, and status in that order. Forms organize related fields in named sections and keep their form footer visible outside scrollable content.

Action bars place Create, Open/Edit, Duplicate, workflow actions, and destructive actions on the left. Refresh is always on the right. Form footers always place Save/Apply at the far right. Destructive actions are technically marked, use object-specific labels, and require confirmation when they change data.

Selection-dependent actions are disabled without an applicable record. Double-click performs the same open or edit operation as the corresponding button. Pages, sections, action bars, form footers, important grids, and actions have stable technical widget IDs for tests and Enterprise acceptance.

The permitted hierarchy has exactly three levels: IconNavbar parent, child work tab, and at most one functional subtab level inside a page. Functional subtabs are reserved for at least two independent peer workflows; semantic groups structure fields inside a workflow.

docs.title: Asynchronous UI, lazy tabs and background services
1. Design rules
docs.text:
The Qt event loop must remain responsive while SQLite queries, backups, signature verification and tachograph processing run. Three rules enforce this:

  1. The Qt main thread constructs and changes widgets/models only.
  2. Database, file, network and CPU work runs in workers or dedicated services.
  3. Invisible workspaces and detail tabs are constructed and loaded only when needed.
flowchart LR
    U["User input"] --> Q["Qt main thread"]
    Q --> L["Lazy-tab factory"]
    Q --> J["UiJobController"]
    J --> R["Read pool: 4"]
    J --> W["Write lane: 1"]
    J --> P["Prefetch lane: 1"]
    R --> D["Worker-owned SQLite connection"]
    W --> D
    P --> D
    D --> C["DTO / list / dictionary"]
    C --> Q
    B["Background services"] --> A["Activity registry"]
    J --> A
    A --> S["Status bar"]
    H["UI heartbeat"] --> S

docs.title: 2. Startup order
docs.text:
The application applies a pending restore, runs central versioned database bootstrap, opens runtime repositories with ensure_schema=False, installs UiJobController and UiHeartbeatMonitor, creates the window, authenticates the user, loads only the visible start view and then starts background services.

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as QApplication
    participant Restore as Pending restore
    participant Bootstrap as DB bootstrap
    participant Jobs as UiJobController
    participant Window as MainWindow
    participant Services as Background services

    App->>Restore: Verify marker and atomically replace if present
    App->>Bootstrap: Configure WAL and run migrations once
    Bootstrap-->>App: quick_check = ok
    App->>Jobs: Install pools and heartbeat
    App->>Window: Build UI without runtime DDL
    Window->>Services: Start timers, backup and optional REST
    Window->>Jobs: Load visible view only

docs.title: 3. Lazy tabs
docs.text:
FileWidget._add_lazy_tab() stores a lightweight placeholder and factory. On currentChanged, the previous page is asked to cancel_load(), a QSignalBlocker prevents recursion, the factory creates the real widget, and the placeholder is replaced at the same index. ensure_loaded() then starts one data job if required.

Vehicle deadlines, costs, invoices, tachograph references, M files, activities, events, speed, technical data, calibrations, positions and audit are lazy. Constructors must not perform large queries. Each page should provide a stable job key, ensure_loaded() and cancel_load().

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Placeholder
    Placeholder --> Constructing: tab activated
    Constructing --> LoadedWidget: factory completes
    LoadedWidget --> LoadingData: ensure_loaded / refresh
    LoadingData --> Ready: current job succeeds
    LoadingData --> Cancelled: tab changed or closed
    Cancelled --> LoadingData: activated again
    Ready --> LoadingData: refresh
    Ready --> Disposed: record rebuilt

docs.title: 4. UiJobController
docs.text:
A UiJobSpec defines a stable key, visible name, work(token, report), lane, priority and metadata. Read jobs use a four-thread pool. Writes are serialised through one worker. Prefetch has one worker.

Submitting the same key cancels the previous token and increments a generation. Signals are delivered only when handle, generation and key are still current. Destroying the owner cancels its token, so an old slow result cannot update a new or closed view.

JobProgress reports text, phase and optional current/total. JobResult includes request ID, duration and metadata such as wait time, phase time, record count and cache hit. Workers return thread-neutral values only; no widget, model or other QObject may cross the worker boundary.

sequenceDiagram
    participant View
    participant Controller as UiJobController
    participant Pool as Worker pool
    participant DB as SQLite

    View->>Controller: submit(key, next generation)
    Controller->>Controller: cancel old token for key
    Controller->>Pool: start QRunnable
    Pool->>DB: open connection in worker
    DB-->>Pool: rows / DTOs
    Pool->>Controller: success(request_id, result)
    Controller->>Controller: validate key, generation and token
    Controller-->>View: emit only current result
    View->>View: update model in Qt thread

docs.title: 5. Worker database pattern
docs.text:
Every worker opens and closes its own connection through the shared runtime factory. Connections are never passed from the UI thread. Schema changes belong to startup bootstrap only.

def work(token, report):
    token.throw_if_cancelled()
    repo = VehicleUnitRepository(db_path, ensure_schema=False)
    report(JobProgress("Loading calibrations", phase="query"))
    rows = repo.list_vehicle_facts("ddd_vu_calibration", vehicle_id, lower, upper, limit, offset)
    token.throw_if_cancelled()
    return [dict(row) for row in rows]

Write jobs commit in the write lane and trigger a new read job only after commit. Filters are captured before worker submission, and large result sets are paginated.

docs.title: 6. Background services and status
docs.text:
BackgroundActivityRegistry is a thread-safe map from stable task key to display text and optional progress. Every service must clear its entry in finally. The status bar polls at 400 ms and prioritises shutdown, active/recent UI stall, background work, transient messages and finally Background: ready.

The BackupCoordinator owns one daemon thread and one non-reentrant run lock. A cycle handles small batches: up to 5 tachograph archives, 20 local financial migrations, 20 financial backups, 10 REST export retries and 50 remote presence checks, plus a due database snapshot. Backup progress pauses in 100-ms increments while a user write job is waiting. SQLite backup uses small page batches; network transfer and read-back occur outside functional transactions.

The scheduler and notification timer runs every 30 seconds. Notification delivery uses a non-blocking lock and daemon worker. Scheduled tasks and the DriverCard REST API run in dedicated threads. Signature re-verification and deadline reconciliation use the serial write lane.

flowchart TD
    A["Service starts"] --> B["Activity registry: set"]
    B --> C{"User write waiting?"}
    C -->|"Yes, backup"| D["Wait briefly and expose status"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Process bounded batch"]
    D --> C
    E --> F["Keep DB transaction short"]
    F --> G["Network/read-back outside transaction"]
    G --> H{"More work?"}
    H -->|"Yes"| E
    H -->|"No/error"| I["Activity registry: clear in finally"]

docs.title: 7. UI heartbeat and UI_STALL
docs.text:
A Qt timer beats every 250 ms. A separate watcher marks UI_STALL after one second without a beat and logs additional main-thread stack samples after 5, 15 and 30 seconds. The log includes delay, active jobs/background tasks and a compact main-thread stack. Recovery is logged on the next beat.

The heartbeat diagnoses blocking; it does not make blocking code asynchronous. A stack ending in SQLite, file or network code in the main thread must be moved to a worker.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Responsive
    Responsive --> Stalled: no beat for 1 s
    Stalled --> Stalled: stack samples at 5/15/30 s
    Stalled --> Recovered: next Qt beat
    Recovered --> Responsive: retention expires

docs.title: 8. Controlled shutdown
docs.text:
System and tray exits share one idempotent path. Normal status timers are stopped and the visible shutdown sequence is: stop scheduler/notification timer, stop DriverCard REST, stop backup coordinator, hide tray, display completion, cancel UiJobs, wait for pools for a bounded period, stop heartbeat, then close Qt.

sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as MainWindow
    participant REST as DriverCard REST
    participant Backup as BackupCoordinator
    participant Jobs as UiJobController
    participant App as QApplication

    User->>UI: Exit
    UI->>UI: Lock shutdown status and stop timers
    UI->>REST: stop()
    UI->>Backup: stop(timeout)
    UI->>Jobs: cancel tokens and clear queues
    Jobs->>Jobs: bounded waitForDone
    UI->>App: close

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting and acceptance
docs.text:
Search app.log for UI_STALL, inspect main_stack, correlate active task names and follow the same request ID through UI_JOB start/success/failed/cancelled. Verify that repositories use ensure_schema=False, result sets are bounded, cancellation is checked between phases and no UI callback performs blocking I/O.

A new page or service is accepted only when construction and tab switching perform no substantial main-thread query, stale results are ignored, worker connections are thread-owned, writes are serial and committed before refresh, activity state is always cleared, shutdown remains idempotent, and navigation remains responsive during parallel backup load.

docs.title: 1. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This document is the technical reference for the SQLite database format used by FLEET Mira storage format V2. It covers the physical database contract, versioned bootstrap, the normalized tachograph fact model, provenance and deduplication, the surrounding business schemas, integrity rules, migration from the legacy format, and supported operational access.

The schema is an internal application contract. Integrations must use the documented application services and APIs for writes. Read-only SQL is useful for diagnostics and controlled reporting, but direct inserts, updates, deletes, schema changes, or trigger changes are unsupported because they can bypass audit, hash verification, derived-data refresh, and migration bookkeeping.

Related documents:

  • Tachograph data parsing, storage and access
  • Asynchronous UI and background services
  • Archiving, backup and restore

docs.title: 2. V2 invariants
docs.text:
Storage format V2 is identified by all of the following conditions:

  1. app_schema_state.storage_format is 2.
  2. ddd_archive has the integer surrogate key archive_pk in addition to the stable public text ID id.
  3. The normalized fact core (ddd_fact_kind, ddd_fact, ddd_fact_source, and all typed payload tables) is complete.
  4. Required fact and card/time indexes exist.
  5. No legacy archive-owned fact table listed by the migration map remains in the database.
  6. The stored schema fingerprint matches the SQL definitions of the V2 archive, fact, payload, and fact-index objects.

The bootstrap rejects a populated ddd_archive table without archive_pk. A legacy database must therefore be rebuilt with the dedicated V2 migration; it is never upgraded in place by normal application startup.

flowchart LR
    S["SQLite file"] --> M["app_schema_state"]
    M --> F{"storage_format = 2"}
    F --> A["ddd_archive.archive_pk"]
    F --> C["normalized fact core"]
    F --> I["required indexes"]
    F --> H["schema fingerprint"]
    A --> V["validate_storage_schema"]
    C --> V
    I --> V
    H --> V

docs.title: 3. Physical SQLite configuration
docs.text:
Setting Runtime value Rationale Page size 8 KiB for newly created databases Reduces B-tree depth and page overhead for the fact store. Journal mode WAL during application runtime Allows readers to continue while the serialized write lane commits. synchronous NORMAL WAL durability/performance balance. Busy timeout 30,000 ms Gives bounded concurrent work time to finish instead of immediately returning SQLITE_BUSY. WAL auto-checkpoint 1,000 pages Bounds WAL growth during ordinary operation. Foreign keys Enabled on every application connection Enforces declared relationships and cascades. Auto-vacuum INCREMENTAL on a new database Permits controlled space reclamation.

The distributable empty database is finalized as a compact single file in DELETE journal mode and vacuumed. Application startup switches it to WAL. The -wal and -shm files are therefore normal runtime companions and must be included in shutdown/checkpoint planning, but not copied independently as a database backup.

PRAGMA user_version is not the migration authority. FLEET Mira uses component rows in app_schema_migration and format state in app_schema_state.

docs.title: 4. Versioned bootstrap
docs.text:
bootstrap_database() is the only supported schema initialization entry point. It runs before the UI and background services construct repositories. Each component migration is recorded once with component, version, UTC application time, and duration.

Component Current bootstrap version Schema owner archive 2 archive metadata, transfer state, and global audit dependencies authentication 1 users, roles, permissions, login security, and UI state device_management 1 devices, tenants, locations, groups, and status history drivercard 2 driver-card import identity and signature evidence fleet 5 persons, vehicles, links, due dates, RFID, licence checks, and notification responsibility routing finance 2 suppliers, invoices, tax summaries, document analysis, costs, financial originals, e-invoices, and exports leasing 2 lease contracts, versioned schedules, recurring invoices, occurrences, and reconciliation vehicle_unit 4 VU import evidence, trust anchors, and normalized V2 fact schema compliance 4 snapshots, rule-module configuration, and immutable catalog metadata backup 1 targets, replication state, jobs, and database snapshots task_execution 1 backend-neutral task runs, source snapshots, and per-file outcomes reporting 3 odometer history, cost-report parameters, and report templates task_execution 1 task runs, source snapshots, file results, and daily report evidence

The version is a per-component migration level, not the product version and not the storage-format number. A schema change must increment the owning component version. After migrations, startup validates V2, calculates its schema fingerprint, updates app_schema_state, commits, and runs PRAGMA quick_check when any migration was applied.

docs.title: Migration ledger
docs.text:
app_schema_migration uses (component, version) as its primary key. app_schema_state is a key/value registry and currently owns at least:

Key Meaning storage_format Physical tachograph storage generation; must equal 2. storage_schema_fingerprint SHA-256 over the normalized schema object's SQL definitions in deterministic order.

If no component migration ran and the calculated fingerprint differs from the registered fingerprint, startup fails. This prevents an unversioned manual DDL change from being silently accepted.

docs.title: 5. High-level data model
docs.text:
erDiagram
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_FACT_SOURCE : contains
    DDD_FACT_KIND ||--o{ DDD_FACT : classifies
    DDD_FACT_KIND ||--o{ DDD_FACT_SOURCE : classifies
    DDD_FACT ||--o{ DDD_FACT_SOURCE : proven_by
    DDD_FACT ||--|| TYPED_PAYLOAD : stores
    DDD_CARD_IDENTITY ||--o{ TYPED_PAYLOAD : normalizes
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT : describes
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT : describes
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_VU_SECTION : segments
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_COMPLIANCE_SNAPSHOT : evaluates
    FLEET_PERSON ||--o{ FLEET_DRIVERCARD_LINK : owns
    FLEET_VEHICLE ||--o{ FLEET_VEHICLE_VU_LINK : owns
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ FLEET_VEHICLE_VU_LINK : links
    FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE ||--o{ FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE_TAX_SUMMARY : taxes
    FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE ||--o{ FLEET_VEHICLE_COST_ENTRY : allocates
    FLEET_FINANCIAL_DOCUMENT }o--|| FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE : evidences
    FLEET_RECURRING_INVOICE ||--o{ FLEET_RECURRING_INVOICE_OCCURRENCE : schedules
    FLEET_LEASE_CONTRACT ||--o{ FLEET_RECURRING_INVOICE : governs
    BACKUP_TARGET ||--o{ BACKUP_ARCHIVE_STATE : replicates

The schema separates four concerns:

  • Evidence: immutable originals, archive metadata, parser/signature records, raw hashes, and audit.
  • Canonical facts: deduplicated observations independent of any one archive.
  • Provenance: every occurrence of a fact in an archive, including section and raw-record identity.
  • Business projections: people, vehicles, due dates, odometers, costs, reports, and backup state derived from or linked to evidence.

docs.title: ddd_archive
docs.text:
ddd_archive is the root for every C- or M-file import.

Column group Important columns Meaning Keys archive_pk, id Internal integer join key and stable public archive ID. File identity file_name, file_name_normalized, file_hash_sha256 Display/search name and SHA-256 of uncompressed DDD bytes. Stored object stored_path, compressed_size, stored_hash_sha256 GZIP object location, size, and hash. Source source_id, task_id, source_host, remote_path, source/download timestamps Transfer provenance. Lifecycle archived_at, is_deleted, deletion actor/time/reason Logical archive lifecycle. Classification ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status Parser and trust outcome. Identity/range identity_label, VIN, registration, data_from, data_to Search and entity-linking projection. Parser result parsed_at, parser_message Last parse attempt.

Active archives are unique by uncompressed file_hash_sha256. Logical deletion preserves the archive and audit row while removing it from active aggregate queries.

docs.title: Parser and signature evidence
docs.text:
Table Purpose ddd_drivercard_import Parsed card identity, generation, holder/licence metadata, parser version, signature summary, and import result. ddd_drivercard_signature Per signed EF block: generation, file ID, algorithm, certificate/trust fingerprints, verification time, and result. ddd_vehicle_unit_import VU generation, VIN, registration, serial, covered range, warnings, signature summary, and correlation ID. ddd_vu_section Section index/code, generation, source byte range, and SHA-256 of the exact signed bytes. ddd_vu_signature Per VU section signature result and certificate evidence. ddd_vu_unknown_record Bounded unsupported records with offsets, raw payload, and 32-byte raw hash so parsing remains loss-aware. tachograph_trust_anchor Versioned trust material used by signature verification.

Archive-owned evidence tables reference the public archive ID and normally use ON DELETE CASCADE. The compressed original remains the authoritative source for a future reparse.

docs.title: Core tables
docs.text:
Table Key Responsibility ddd_fact_kind kind_id Stable registry of typed fact kinds. ddd_card_identity card_pk Deduplicated normalized card number plus the best display form. ddd_fact fact_pk One canonical semantic observation, its full hash, cluster hash, kind, and optional event epoch. ddd_fact_source archive/kind/time/ordinal One occurrence of a fact in one archive, including section, record, raw hash, and source-only generation. ddd_fact_<kind> fact_pk Typed payload in compact SQLite-native fields.

ddd_fact_source is a WITHOUT ROWID table. Its composite primary key is ordered for deterministic per-archive replacement. It references ddd_archive, ddd_fact_kind, and ddd_fact; deleting an archive cascades its source rows. Orphan canonical facts are removed explicitly after archive replacement or removal.

docs.title: Encodings
docs.text:
Logical value Stored form UTC timestamp Signed integer Unix seconds. Calendar day Integer day offset from 1970-01-01. Activity 0=BREAK_REST, 1=AVAILABILITY, 2=WORK, 3=DRIVING. Card number card_pk into ddd_card_identity. Text Unicode NFC, control-character removal, and collapsed whitespace. Raw digest Exactly 32 bytes. Speed data One BLOB containing the complete 60-second block; 0xFF remains a missing sample.

Card normalization uppercases and retains alphanumeric characters only. All-placeholder values are treated as absent. The longer available display representation wins without changing the normalized identity.

docs.title: Fact and cluster hashes
docs.text:
The canonical fact_hash is SHA-256 over:

  1. ASCII fact-kind name and a zero byte;
  2. deterministic compact JSON of all encoded payload fields, sorted by key;
  3. a zero byte and the raw BLOB for fact kinds such as speed blocks.

UNIQUE(kind_id, fact_hash) stores an identical observation once even when many archives contain it.

The cluster_hash uses only the fact kind's domain-specific cluster fields. It groups records that represent the same logical slot/time/key but may disagree in other values. If a cluster has more than one distinct full fact hash, aggregate queries set has_conflict=true; variants are retained rather than overwritten.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
ddd_fact_source records:

  • archive and kind;
  • source ordinal;
  • canonical fact;
  • event epoch or the reserved no-event sentinel for time-free facts;
  • section index and code;
  • record index;
  • SHA-256 of the exact raw record, or a deterministic fallback hash;
  • card generation when generation belongs to source evidence rather than semantic identity.

This design allows a canonical row to be deduplicated without losing which files, sections, records, or generations proved it.

docs.title: Reparse transaction
docs.text:
For one archive and one fact kind, replace_archive_records() performs:

  1. delete the old ddd_fact_source rows for that archive/kind;
  2. normalize and encode each parser record;
  3. calculate full and cluster hashes;
  4. insert or reuse ddd_fact;
  5. insert the typed payload if this is a new fact;
  6. insert the archive-specific source row;
  7. remove canonical facts no longer referenced by any archive.

The original archive row, signature evidence, and other archives remain unchanged.

docs.title: 8. Fact-kind catalog
docs.text: Kind / payload table Stored semantic fields Cluster identity vu.activity / ddd_fact_vu_activity slot, change time, activity, card-present flag, crew flag, card slot + change time vu.card_session / ddd_fact_vu_card_session slot, card, names, expiry, insert/withdraw times slot + card + insert/withdraw times vu.event / ddd_fact_vu_event type, begin, end type + begin + end vu.fault / ddd_fact_vu_fault type, begin, end type + begin + end vu.overspeed / ddd_fact_vu_overspeed begin/end, maximum and average speed begin + end vu.speed_block / ddd_fact_vu_speed_block start epoch, 60-byte speed BLOB start epoch vu.technical / ddd_fact_vu_technical record type, value, detail JSON record type vu.calibration / ddd_fact_vu_calibration purpose, workshop, VIN, registration, calibration times purpose + calibration time vu.position / ddd_fact_vu_position position type, time, coordinates, raw hex type + time vu.border / ddd_fact_vu_border crossing time, coordinates, raw hex crossing time vu.load / ddd_fact_vu_load time, operation, coordinates, raw hex time + operation vu.odometer / ddd_fact_vu_odometer source day, midnight time, odometer source day card.activity / ddd_fact_card_activity card, activity, start/end, duration, day, crew, slot card + start/end + slot card.event / ddd_fact_card_event card, event codes/text, begin/end, vehicle, place card + numeric type + begin/end card.fault / ddd_fact_card_fault card, fault codes/text, begin/end, vehicle, place card + numeric type + begin/end card.vehicle / ddd_fact_card_vehicle card, use interval, odometers, distance, registration, VIN, block counter card + use interval + registration card.position / ddd_fact_card_position card, source, record/position times, country/region, odometer, coordinates, accuracy, authentication card + source + record/position times

docs.title: Aggregate queries
docs.text:
list_facts() returns one canonical fact across a caller-supplied archive scope. It:

  • ignores logically deleted archives;
  • filters by ddd_fact.event_epoch;
  • returns source count and archive IDs;
  • chooses a preferred source by verified parse/signature status, then generation (G2_V2, G2_V1, older), then newest archive;
  • reports conflicting variants by cluster;
  • caps a page at 1,000,000 rows.

docs.title: Single-archive queries
docs.text: list_archive_observations() starts at ddd_fact_source, preserves the source ordinal, section/record identity, raw hash, and generation, and returns only observations from that file. It deliberately does not collapse repeated source records.

docs.title: Required indexes
docs.text:
• ix_ddd_fact_kind_time supports kind/time pagination.
  • ix_ddd_fact_source_fact supports source aggregation and orphan checks.
  • Card-bearing, time-bearing payloads have (card_pk, time, fact_pk) indexes.
  • Archive search indexes cover active hash uniqueness, type/date, parse/signature status, normalized name, and archive time.

Indexes are dropped during bulk V2 rebuild and recreated only after all archives have been reparsed, followed by ANALYZE and PRAGMA optimize.

docs.title: 10. Compliance and audit
docs.text:
ddd_compliance_snapshot stores immutable, reproducible evaluation output: archive or subject scope, assessed range, ruleset and algorithm versions, source manifest, module manifest, configuration hash, report JSON, report SHA-256, creator, and time. Triggers reject updates and deletes.

compliance_rule_module_config stores the global enabled state and JSON settings per rule module. compliance_balm_catalog stores immutable catalog-version metadata; triggers reject update and delete operations.

Audit is split by responsibility:

Table Scope audit_log Global user, administration, and cross-domain actions. ddd_audit_log Archive, parser, signature, export, and tachograph lifecycle. fleet_audit_log Fleet, deadline, RFID, finance, and related business objects.

Audit rows store technical object IDs and actors. They are append-oriented and are resolved by the UI to the current business record.

docs.text:
Tables Purpose fleet_person, fleet_vehicle Person and vehicle master records with logical archival. fleet_drivercard_link Unique card-to-person assignment and source archive evidence. fleet_vehicle_vu_link Vehicle-to-M-file assignment, match basis, and confirmation state. fleet_mobile_device Fleet-related mobile-device assignments. fleet_due_type, fleet_due Configurable person/vehicle deadlines and managed download schedules; vehicle rows support time, mileage and earliest-of-both limits with captured completion evidence. fleet_license_check Driving-licence check results. fleet_rfid_assignment Current and historical RFID-to-person assignments. fleet_rfid_import_file, fleet_rfid_import_row Imported terminal files, row fingerprints, validation, and processing results.

Open tachograph download schedules are protected by a partial unique index on object, manager, and active state. Active RFID UIDs and current person assignments are also unique.

docs.title: Finance and e-invoices
docs.text:
Tables Purpose fleet_supplier Supplier identity, contact, tax, VAT, endpoint, and company identifiers. fleet_cost_category Cost classification and fixed/variable defaults. fleet_foreign_invoice Invoice, credit-note or recurring-invoice header, source, dates, totals, optional uniform VAT rate, workflow, duplicate override, reversal, and audit actors. fleet_foreign_invoice_tax_summary Authoritative VAT category, basis, tax and gross totals for uniform and mixed-rate documents. fleet_vehicle_cost_entry Vehicle/category allocation, validity period, signed amounts, tax, workflow, reversal, recurring-occurrence and reclassification links. fleet_lease_contract Vehicle/supplier lease terms, factor inputs, authoritative actual rate, mileage evidence and lifecycle. fleet_lease_component Recurring and one-time contract components, including effective-factor relevance. fleet_lease_schedule_item Versioned planned payment schedule with stable instalment identity across contract changes. fleet_lease_document_link Links a contract to immutable documents from its vehicle record. fleet_lease_cost_link Links actual vehicle cost or credit positions, including invoice positions, to a contract. fleet_recurring_invoice Immutable recurring-invoice assignment, repeating amounts, active period, posting mode and contract/schedule references. fleet_recurring_invoice_mode_change Audited effective-dated AUTO/MANUAL changes that affect only future unposted periods. fleet_recurring_invoice_occurrence Idempotent monthly due item, reconciliation state, worker outcome and resulting cost entry. fleet_financial_document Local original/manifest identity, SHA-256, archive status, optional backup state, retention, legal hold, and supersession. fleet_document Versioned personnel/vehicle record documents with SHA-256 verified local archive, backup identity, archive lifecycle and controlled purge evidence. fleet_einvoice_import Syntax/profile, original/XML hashes, validator result, documents, supplier match, contract reference and object references. fleet_einvoice_line Structured source lines and adjustments with exact monetary values and allocation status. fleet_einvoice_allocation Cent-accurate line split into vehicle cost entries, including confirmed suggestions. fleet_invoice_document_analysis Versioned supplier-invoice-v1 local/cloud findings, confidence, evidence and explicit cloud consent. fleet_invoice_match_feedback Confirmed and corrected matching signals used by local learning. fleet_ai_connector_provider Shared Azure/Vertex provider, region, model, credential reference and connection-test state; secrets remain outside the database. fleet_finance_export Durable accounting export/outbox state, correction kind and retries. fleet_finance_settings Finance/export/report calculation settings.

Money uses integer cents; VAT rates use integer basis points. Reversal objects retain links to their originals. A non-overridden active invoice is unique by supplier, case-insensitive document number, and document date. Original files live in the financial archive, not in SQLite; the database stores paths, hashes, sizes, manifests, and state.

docs.title: Odometer and reporting
docs.text:
Tables Purpose fleet_vehicle_odometer_reading M-, C-, manual, and imported readings with source, quality, approval, and archive link. fleet_report_template Versioned system/user report templates, context, ownership, defaults, and JSON definition.

M-file midnight readings are authoritative. Manual and C-file values may fill missing boundaries but cannot replace a valid M value. Cost/km is calculated from complete vehicle-month intersections rather than persisted as an uncontrolled aggregate.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
Tables Purpose backup_target Provider, root, active state, protected credentials/key, encryption, and health timestamps. backup_archive_state Per-target tachograph archive replication state, attempts, hashes, and next retry. backup_database_snapshot Snapshot hashes, sizes, remote identity, retention class, verification, and correlation ID. backup_job Coarse-grained run progress and result.

A partial unique index permits only one active backup target. Backup metadata does not replace the local archive state in ddd_archive or fleet_financial_document.

docs.title: 13. Legacy-to-V2 migration
docs.text:
The supported migration is an out-of-place rebuild performed by scripts/migrate_demo_database_v2.py.

flowchart TD
    A["Legacy database"] --> B["Preflight quick/FK checks"]
    B --> C["Verify every GZIP and original DDD hash"]
    C --> D["Bootstrap empty V2 work database"]
    D --> E["Copy authoritative business rows"]
    E --> F["Reparse every active C/M original"]
    F --> G["Rebuild odometers and download due dates"]
    G --> H["Compare counts, distinct facts, ranges, speed digests, signatures"]
    H --> I["Create indexes, ANALYZE, optimize, FK/quick checks"]
    I --> J["VACUUM and size check"]
    J --> K{"--apply"}
    K -->|"no"| L["Keep validated candidate"]
    K -->|"yes"| M["Rename source to V1 backup, candidate to source"]

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
• source exists and is not already V2;
  • work database, WAL, and SHM do not exist;
  • a requested backup target does not already exist;
  • free space is at least 512 MiB or 110% of source size, whichever is larger;
  • source quick_check and foreign_key_check pass;
  • each active C/M archive has a readable GZIP object;
  • stored-object and uncompressed-original SHA-256 values match the archive row.

docs.title: Rebuild
docs.text: Authoritative business tables are copied by common column name. Derived tachograph tables, migration state, audit projections, automatically managed download due dates, and non-manual odometer projections are rebuilt. Active archives are reparsed from original bytes into the new fact model. Fact indexes are created after bulk loading.

docs.title: Semantic validation
docs.text:
For every fact kind the migration compares:

  • observation count;
  • distinct semantic count;
  • minimum and maximum event time;
  • per-archive observation counts;
  • exact expanded speed-byte count and digest;
  • archive signature status.

It then validates the schema, foreign keys, quick check, 8 KiB page size, and post-vacuum database. A large source must meet the migration's compaction threshold.

docs.title: Atomic activation
docs.text: --apply is refused while source WAL/SHM files exist. The source is renamed to the V1 backup, then the validated candidate is renamed to the source path. If the second rename fails, the backup is restored. The V1 backup is not deleted automatically.

docs.title: 14. Deployment database contract
docs.text:
scripts/create_deployment_database.py creates a fresh V2 database, validates integrity and foreign keys, validates the storage schema and 8 KiB page size, confirms format 2, and verifies the expected seed counts. Business tables must be empty. The initial administrator is active, uses English/en-GB, and must change the initial password.
