After validation, the database is vacuumed into one file and accompanied by archive.db.sha256. Release tooling must verify that checksum against the exact database file after the final write.

docs.title: 15. Operational checks
docs.text:
Use a read-only connection for diagnostics:

SELECT key, value
FROM app_schema_state
ORDER BY key;

SELECT component, version, applied_at, duration_ms
FROM app_schema_migration
ORDER BY component, version;

PRAGMA quick_check;
PRAGMA foreign_key_check;

Fact counts and provenance:

SELECT k.name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.fact_pk) AS canonical_facts,
       COUNT(s.fact_pk) AS source_observations,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.archive_pk) AS source_archives
FROM ddd_fact_kind k
LEFT JOIN ddd_fact f ON f.kind_id = k.kind_id
LEFT JOIN ddd_fact_source s ON s.fact_pk = f.fact_pk
GROUP BY k.kind_id, k.name
ORDER BY k.kind_id;

Archive health:

SELECT ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status, COUNT(*) AS archives
FROM ddd_archive
WHERE is_deleted = 0
GROUP BY ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status
ORDER BY ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status;

Do not use diagnostic SQL to repair data. Restore a verified database or re-run the owning import, migration, reconciliation, or rebuild service so hashes, provenance, audit, and projections remain consistent.

docs.title: Tachograph data parsing, storage and access
1. Scope and guarantees
docs.text:
This document describes the technical path of driver-card C files and vehicle-unit M files from the immutable DDD original through parsing, signature verification, database storage, cross-archive deduplication and repository access.

  • The compressed DDD original is the auditable source of truth.
  • Archive, signature, section and raw-record evidence remains archive-specific.
  • Reparsing replaces only derived observations for that archive.
  • person and vehicle aggregate views deduplicate across every linked archive.
  • A single-archive view still reproduces only that file's observations.
  • Deduplication never changes parser or signature status.
flowchart LR
    A["DDD input"] --> B["Local GZIP original"]
    B --> C["Archive metadata and SHA-256"]
    B --> D{"Binary classification"}
    D -->|"C file"| E["DriverCardFullParser"]
    D -->|"M file"| F["VehicleUnitParser"]
    E --> G["C signature verification"]
    F --> H["M signature verification"]
    G --> I["Archive-specific C tables"]
    H --> J["Archive-specific M tables"]
    I --> K["Canonical aggregate view"]
    J --> K
    K --> L["Repository"]
    L --> M["UI / reporting / compliance"]
    I --> N["Single-archive view"]
    J --> N

docs.title: 2. Archive and common import pipeline
docs.text:
ddd_archive holds the archive ID, file name, original and stored hashes, storage path, sizes, source, timestamps, DDD type, generation, parse/signature status, identity fields and covered date range.

TachographImportService.import_archive_id() performs these steps:

  1. Load the archive row and reject a logically deleted archive unless explicitly allowed.
  2. Read the DDD bytes from the GZIP object.
  3. Classify the binary content; the file name is not authoritative.
  4. Record classification and an audit event under a new correlation ID.
  5. Run the C or M parser.
  6. Verify exact signed bytes against the trust store.
  7. Replace archive-specific derived observations and update archive status.
  8. Reconcile entity links, download deadlines and cached evaluations.
Column Content Purpose file_hash_sha256 SHA-256 of uncompressed DDD bytes proves the original functional content stored_hash_sha256 SHA-256 of the stored GZIP object detects storage damage or modification 
sequenceDiagram
    participant Import as TachographImportService
    participant Archive as ddd_archive
    participant File as GZIP original
    participant Parser as C/M parser
    participant Verify as Signature service
    participant DB as Observation tables

    Import->>Archive: Load archive metadata
    Import->>File: Read exact DDD bytes
    Import->>Parser: Classify and parse
    Parser-->>Import: Structure, identity and source references
    Import->>Verify: Verify signed blocks/sections
    Verify-->>Import: VALID / INVALID / UNVERIFIABLE / MISSING
    Import->>DB: Replace observations for archive
    Import->>Archive: Update generation, range and status

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text:
DriverCardFullParser preserves every EF and signature boundary. Each segment has a five-byte header: two-byte file ID, one-byte kind (0 G1 data, 1 G1 signature, 2 G2 data, 3 G2 signature), and a two-byte big-endian length. Payloads extending past the file or trailing bytes after the last segment are parse errors. Offset, length and SHA-256 are calculated for every payload.

Important EFs include:

EF Data 0501, 0525 application identification, generation and record counts 0520, 0521 card holder and driving-licence identity 0504 daily driver activity 0502, 0503 events and faults 0505 vehicles used and odometers 0506, 0524 places and GNSS positions 0526–0530 G2V2 authentication, borders and loading data C100, C101, C108, C109 card, CardSign, CA and link certificates

Generation is derived as G1, G2 or G2V2 and mapped to G1, G2_V1 or G2_V2 in the archive row.

The activity ring buffer is followed by its oldest/newest pointers. Daily-record headers and payloads are read cyclically, so a record may start in the final EF bytes and continue at offset zero; traversal stops only after the record identified by activityPointerNewestRecord. A length-guided linear scan is the guarded fallback. Daily records are deduplicated by date and presence counter. Minute changes become intervals for BREAK_REST, AVAILABILITY, WORK and DRIVING. Event/fault arrays use counts from application identification. Vehicle, place and GNSS records retain timestamps, registration, VIN where present, odometers, coordinates, accuracy and authentication state. Empty records are not emitted.

flowchart TD
    A["C file bytes"] --> B["Validate segment headers and boundaries"]
    B --> C["Build EF segments with offset and SHA-256"]
    C --> D["Read application identification"]
    D --> E["Determine generation and record counts"]
    E --> F["Identity and card metadata"]
    E --> G["Activity ring buffer"]
    E --> H["Events and faults"]
    E --> I["Vehicles, places and GNSS"]
    F --> J["Normalised observations"]
    G --> J
    H --> J
    I --> J
    J --> K["Verify signed EFs"]
    K --> L["Replace archive-specific C rows"]

docs.title: 4. M-file parser
docs.text:
Every section starts with 0x76 and a TREP code.

Generation TREP codes Logical sections G1 01–05 overview, activities, events/faults, speed, technical G2 v1 21–25 the same areas encoded as RecordArrays G2 v2 31–35 G2-v2 records including additional GNSS/border/load data

Mixed generations, impossible lengths, data after a signature, or incomplete mandatory structures fail parsing. A missing detailed-speed section is an optional-download warning, not a signature error.

G1 uses fixed or count-driven structures followed by a 128-byte signature. Two 194-byte certificates at the start of the overview are excluded from the signed data as required by Annex IB. VIN is read as 17 characters. Country and code-page bytes are skipped before the 13-character registration number. The covered range comes from VuDownloadablePeriod, not current VU time.

G2 uses RecordArrays with type, size and count. size × count is checked before reading. Certificate records (0x04, 0x0F) and the single signature record (0x08) remain separate from functional records. Each functional record receives section index/code, record index and SHA-256 of exact bytes.

Both paths decode identity, covered period, activities, card sessions, events, faults, overspeed, speed, technical/calibration, position, border, load and midnight-odometer observations. Unknown bounded records remain available as raw evidence and warnings.

docs.title: Compact speed storage
docs.text:
All generations use ddd_vu_speed_block: Unix start_epoch, exactly 60 speed bytes including 0xFF, and one binary 32-byte source SHA-256. 0xFF stays in the stored block but is omitted from measurement results. Date filtering, offset and limit apply after second-by-second expansion.

flowchart TD
    A["M file bytes"] --> B{"TREP generation"}
    B -->|"G1"| C["Fixed/count-driven sections"]
    B -->|"G2 v1/v2"| D["Validate RecordArrays"]
    C --> E["Separate signed body and 128-byte signature"]
    D --> F["Separate certificates, records and signature"]
    E --> G["Normalise observations"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["SHA-256 per source record"]
    G --> I["60-second speed blocks"]
    H --> J["Verify each section"]
    I --> J
    J --> K["Replace archive-specific M rows"]

docs.title: 5. Signature model
docs.text:
tachograph_trust_anchor stores generation, key ID, SHA-256 fingerprint, certificate/key material, validity, revocation, source and active state.

  • C G1 uses card/CA certificates and RSA PKCS#1 with SHA-1 over exact data blocks.
  • C G2/G2V2 uses CardSign/MSCA and optional link certificates with ECDSA over signed EFs.
  • M G1 uses RSA PKCS#1/SHA-1; M G2 verifies each section with its certificate-defined ECC/hash chain.
  • Per-block results are in ddd_drivercard_signature; per-section results are in ddd_vu_signature.

The newest plausible signed functional timestamp is the certificate reference time. Archive time is a warned fallback. Overall precedence is INVALID, UNVERIFIABLE, MISSING, then VALID.

docs.title: Archive and evidence
docs.text: ddd_archive, ddd_audit_log, fleet_audit_log, tachograph_trust_anchor and app_schema_migration preserve source, audit, trust and schema-version information.

docs.title: C tables
docs.text: ddd_drivercard_import, ddd_drivercard_activity, ddd_drivercard_event, ddd_drivercard_fault, ddd_drivercard_vehicle_used, ddd_drivercard_position and ddd_drivercard_signature hold typed archive observations. Legacy-compatible raw_json and source_json columns remain but new imports store NULL because all required values can be reproduced from the original and typed columns.

docs.title: M tables
docs.text:
ddd_vehicle_unit_import, ddd_vu_section, ddd_vu_signature, ddd_vu_raw_record, the activity/session/event/fault/overspeed tables, ddd_vu_speed_block, technical/calibration tables, position/border/load tables, and ddd_vu_odometer_midnight hold typed observations. ddd_vu_technical.details_json stores the complete structured VU identification used by the field tree. fleet_vehicle_vu_link links every matching M archive to a vehicle master record.

erDiagram
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT : "is C file"
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT : "is M file"
    DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_DRIVERCARD_ACTIVITY : contains
    DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_DRIVERCARD_SIGNATURE : proves
    DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_VU_SECTION : contains
    DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_VU_SPEED_BLOCK : contains
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_FACT_PROVENANCE : supplies
    DDD_CANONICAL_FACT ||--o{ DDD_FACT_PROVENANCE : sourced_by
    DDD_FACT_KIND ||--o{ DDD_CANONICAL_FACT : types

Important indexes cover archive name/date/type/status, normalised card number plus generation, archive/time and card/time activity access, vehicle/archive links, and canonical fact time/cluster/provenance. ddd_vu_speed_block is WITHOUT ROWID; its primary key beginning with archive and start time is already the required access path.

Runtime connections use WAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=30000, synchronous=NORMAL and a 1,000-page automatic checkpoint. Schema work runs once before UI creation; repositories open with ensure_schema=False during normal operation.

docs.title: 7. Cross-archive deduplication
docs.text:
Archive-specific typed tables remain exact provenance. Aggregate views use one of two compatible paths:

  1. Materialised ddd_canonical_fact and ddd_fact_provenance rows.
  2. A compact SQL fallback over typed tables using ROW_NUMBER, COUNT and GROUP_CONCAT when no materialised provenance exists.

The compact production migration deliberately uses the fallback to avoid duplicating all payloads. Both paths return source count, source archive IDs and preferred navigation source.

Materialised normalisation uses Unicode NFC/collapsed whitespace, alphanumeric uppercase identifiers, UTC seconds, exact numeric/coordinate values and exact blobs. Placeholder-only identifiers are empty. fact_hash is a binary SHA-256 over kind and full normalised content; cluster_hash hashes identifying cluster fields. Variants in one cluster remain separate and can be marked as conflicts.

For card observations, the complete normalised card number is the only cross-archive and cross-source identity. card_generation remains source metadata in the raw observation and provenance, but is neither part of the fact hash nor a C/M matching filter. G1 card/G1 vehicle, G1 card/G2 vehicle, G2 card/G1 vehicle and G2 card/G2 vehicle combinations are therefore handled identically.

The fallback partitions by every functional field. Navigation preference is verified/valid, then G2 v2, G2 v1, G1, then newest archive. This never changes functional content. Speed blocks partition by start epoch and the complete 60-byte blob before expansion.

Vehicle technical data is deduplicated by record type, value and the complete normalised detail structure. Existing rows without details_json are reconstructed in a worker from the immutable compressed M original. The vehicle record shows each identical variant once with its source count; archive identifiers and file names remain navigation metadata. New imports persist details_json directly and include it in the technical fact hash.

flowchart TD
    A["Vehicle or person"] --> B["Resolve linked active archives"]
    B --> C{"Materialised provenance exists?"}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Select fact_hash and group sources"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Partition typed rows with window functions"]
    D --> F["Detect cluster variants"]
    E --> G["Select exact duplicate representative"]
    F --> H["Apply date filter"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["Sort, limit and offset"]
    I --> J["DTOs for UI/reporting"]

docs.title: 8. Repository access
docs.text:
list_vehicle_facts, count_vehicle_facts, list_vehicle_speed_seconds, list_person_facts, and list_archive_observations are the primary internal interfaces. Aggregate access resolves linked archives, deduplicates, filters, sorts and only then paginates. Single-archive access filters directly by archive ID and preserves section/record order.

UI calls execute through UiJobController workers. Each worker opens its own SQLite connection and returns only lists, dictionaries or DTOs. Widgets and models are updated only by the UI-thread callback.

docs.title: 9. Idempotency, migration and diagnostics
docs.text:
Reimport replaces derived rows for one archive. Parser failure does not discard previously verified details. Maintenance migration operates on a SQLite copy, verifies every original/hash and count, removes JSON caches, compacts with VACUUM INTO, runs PRAGMA quick_check, and performs an atomic or next-start staged replacement with a rollback backup.

Administrators may use read-only checks such as:

PRAGMA quick_check;
PRAGMA journal_mode;

SELECT component, version, applied_at, duration_ms
FROM app_schema_migration ORDER BY component;

SELECT ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status, COUNT(*)
FROM ddd_archive WHERE is_deleted = 0
GROUP BY ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status;

Direct database writes are unsupported; use import, reparse, link, migration and restore services so audit, hashes and cache invalidation remain consistent.

docs.title: Cost analysis and reporting
docs.text:
The Cost analysis workspace evaluates booked vehicle costs only. Credits and reversal entries retain their accounting sign. Users can select net or gross amounts.

Open the workspace through Fleet management > Fleet > Cost analysis. By default, a newly opened analysis covers January 1 of the current year through today. Administrators can select the last twelve months or a configurable rolling number of days as the global default under Administration > Cost analysis > Calculation parameters. A changed default applies the next time the cost analysis is opened; filters already edited in an open workspace remain unchanged.

Choose period, optional vehicle, All/Fixed/Variable, net or gross and a report template, then select Refresh analysis. Total cost is the period-allocated booked cost including credits and cancellations. It is the TCO data basis for the selected period; it is not claimed to be lifetime-complete when categories or periods are missing.

The KPI strip separates Total cost, eligible cost, eligible kilometres, cost/km and data basis. Total cost remains complete while cost/km uses only jointly reliable vehicle-months.

docs.title: Mileage basis
docs.text:
M files provide an end-of-day odometer value for each included UTC day. FLEET Mira stores it at the following day's 00:00 UTC boundary. Vehicle-use, place and three-hour GNSS records from C files supplement the history.

Cost analysis and mileage reports use the same OdometerBoundaryResolver. Only qualified VALID or WARNING readings are eligible; manual, unknown, unverified and conflicting values are excluded.

Source priority is:

  1. signature-valid M-file midnight reading;
  2. GPS-server telematics sensor;
  3. C-file vehicle use;
  4. C-file place;
  5. C-file three-hour GNSS;
  6. GPS-server telematics GPS.

Cost per kilometre is calculated at vehicle-month level. The first and last month are clipped to the selected range. A vehicle-month is included only when it contains at least one cost entry, reliable period boundaries and positive mileage. Missing boundaries follow the same administrative rule as mileage reports: incomplete, interpolated or bounded extrapolation. For a missing opening boundary, the central policy can extrapolate backwards from the first qualified following days; for a missing closing boundary, it projects forwards from preceding readings. During the current local day, an available qualified actual reading is used; otherwise the central policy can extrapolate up to the current calculation instant. The same estimated mileage is therefore available to cost/km. Opening and closing readings are rounded to whole kilometres first; the difference is then exactly closing minus opening. The Odometer readings per vehicle and day report exposes the same boundaries and estimation supports for direct audit.

Total cost continues to include every cost in the selected range. Eligible cost, eligible mileage and cost/km include matching vehicle-months only. Vehicles or months without costs or mileage therefore no longer suppress metrics for complete subsets.

Coverage is shown as eligible cost-bearing vehicle-months. The column heading explains the metric generally; each value's tooltip states the actual number of cost and eligible months and lists the vehicle's concrete monthly mileage warnings. The interface displays Complete for full coverage, Partial for a usable subset, and Mileage data missing when costs exist without a cost/km basis. No costs and No data identify individual vehicles or months without costs or without either data type.

Import tachograph data reparses older M archives that do not yet contain extracted daily odometer values. Values that cannot be matched uniquely by VIN or registration remain visible for resolution.

Under Administration > Cost analysis > Odometer history, filter by vehicle, import older tachograph data or enter a manual reading. Manual readings require timestamp, value and note and rank below M-file midnight readings.

docs.title: Cost rules
docs.text:
• Variable costs belong to the period containing their document date.
  • Fixed costs are allocated by day across their validity range.
  • Fixed costs without a complete validity range produce a data-quality warning.
  • Vehicle-months with mileage but no cost entry are not treated as zero-cost input for the fleet ratio.
  • Entries that net to zero still count as an existing cost basis.
  • When an entry is cancelled, the cancelled original and its booked counter-entry are evaluated together and therefore net to zero.
  • Comparisons cover the immediately preceding equal-length period and the previous-year period.

docs.title: Views and KPIs
docs.text:
• Vehicles shows fixed, variable and total cost, eligible subset, kilometres, cost/km, coverage and quality per vehicle.
  • Categories identifies the categories driving the TCO data basis.
  • Trend compares monthly values including cost/km and coverage.
  • Comparisons contrasts current period, direct predecessor and prior year and evaluates changes using the administrative materiality threshold.
  • Bookings lists included entries with vehicle, supplier, category and allocated amount.
  • Data quality explains missing boundaries, unassigned mileage and incomplete fixed-cost periods.

docs.title: Stimulsoft
docs.text:
View report opens the local Reports.JS viewer. Export requires finance.reporting.export. Users with reporting.templates.write can clone a system template and edit the copy. System templates remain immutable.

The Reports.JS runtime is loaded from assets/stimulsoft or STIMULSOFT_ASSET_DIR. Licensing is read only from STIMULSOFT_LICENSE_KEY or STIMULSOFT_LICENSE_FILE.

The report host listens on 127.0.0.1 only and uses a random session token for each opened report.

docs.title: Deadlines and record documents
docs.text: Deadlines and documents are maintained directly against a person or vehicle record. Both use stable object IDs, permission checks and record-level audit events, so the complete history remains available from the related record.

docs.title: Evaluate deadlines
docs.text:
Open Fleet management → Personnel → Deadline evaluation or Fleet → Deadline evaluation. Search and filters cover object, due type, state, basis, trigger, mileage quality, evaluability and date range.

Figure: Filterable personnel deadlines with lead-time and completion states.

Status colours distinguish items outside the lead period, approaching or due today, overdue and completed. Printing, print preview and PDF include only the visible filtered rows and columns.

docs.title: Time and mileage rules
docs.text:
Personnel deadlines are time-based. Vehicle deadlines may use:

  • Time: due date, time lead and optional time recurrence;
  • Odometer: target mileage, mileage lead and optional mileage recurrence;
  • Earliest of both: the first reached limit determines the state and completion trigger.

The evaluation shows the latest reliable odometer reading, its timestamp and source, target and remaining mileage, trigger and data quality. Without a valid reading, a combined deadline keeps its time evaluation but marks the mileage part as partial. A mileage-only deadline remains not evaluable until a reliable reading exists.

System-managed download and driving-licence deadlines cannot be moved or completed manually. Their source workflow updates them automatically.

docs.title: Maintain a record document
docs.text:
1. Open a person or vehicle record and select Documents.
  2. Add a file by selection or drag-and-drop.
  3. Enter title, document date, type and optional notes.
  4. Review Valid until. A new value is calculated from the document date and the configured record-document retention period.
  5. Save and verify the preview for PDF or image documents.

Figure: An anonymised person record containing documents, deadlines, licence checks and audit.

Figure: An anonymised vehicle record containing documents, deadlines, finance and tachodata.

New versions retain the document relationship and history. The byte-identical original is written atomically to the primary document archive. A configured backup job copies and reads it back separately; successful local creation does not claim that an external backup already exists.

docs.title: Archive, restore and purge
docs.text: Logical archiving is available from the document context menu and requires the appropriate write permission. Local restore and permanent purge are restricted administrative actions. Permanent purge requires confirmation and a mandatory reason; the evidence record and audit trail remain.

docs.title: Reports and audit
docs.text: The report dashboard provides Personnel deadlines and Fleet deadlines. Fleet reports additionally include time/mileage basis, trigger, odometer quality and evaluability. Every create, change, completion, archive, document view, restore and purge operation is represented in global and record-level audit.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: State Action Mileage deadline is not evaluable Import/link a current M file or add a verified manual odometer reading. Combined deadline shows partial The time result is valid; investigate the missing or implausible mileage reading. Valid-until date is unexpected Check document date, region display and the separate record-document retention setting. Document preview is unavailable Verify the file type and open the byte-identical original with an authorised local application. Backup is still pending Keep the local original; inspect the backup task and worker status instead of adding the document again.

docs.title: Driver-card analysis
docs.text: The analysis is always bound to one selected C file and archive ID. M data is comparison evidence only. Quarantined files remain viewable but cannot feed an effective combined evaluation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Figure: Card identity, validity, authorities, generation and data range.

The header identifies the anonymised driver, card and file. A quarantine banner explains missing or invalid signature verification. Empty values mean that the selected file does not contain the information or it could not be read safely.

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
Figure: Sortable UTC intervals with C/M availability.

Data availability filters all intervals, C and M available, C only or M only. C remains the base. Rows include start, end, duration, activity, card, slot and counterpart archives; double-click and context actions open unambiguous sources.

The single-file view remains archive-scoped. Personnel record > Day/Week/Violations, by contrast, combines all valid card links for that person, including card changes. The heading identifies record or archive scope and must be considered when interpreting totals.

docs.title: Day chart
docs.text:
Figure: One UTC day with driving, work, availability and rest/break.

The date, arrow buttons and Go to change the visible day. The availability track indicates C/M coverage, while activity tracks show business intervals. The detail grid remains sortable.

Read left to right in UTC. Colour and label distinguish driving, other work, availability and rest/break; gaps and overlaps are not smoothed. Hover a segment for start, end, duration, source and availability. Day totals apply to the visible day, not the entire file.

docs.title: Week chart
docs.text:
Figure: ISO week from Monday to Sunday.

Seven UTC days are shown together. Empty days remain visible and are not interpreted as activity. Totals and tooltips refer to the selected file and visible period.

Week arrows move between ISO weeks; Go to selects the week containing a date. Review coverage and card validity first, then daily patterns and weekly totals. An empty or partially covered day is not evidence of rest.

docs.title: DDD week view Web
docs.text:
Figure: Secure in-app entry point to the browser-based week view.

The page starts the local web view through a tokenised hand-off; local archive paths do not appear in its URL. Documentation deliberately does not load a signed original DDD into an external page.

docs.title: Events and faults
docs.text:
Figure: Technical event and fault records.

Codes, periods, vehicles and descriptions come from the selected card. An empty page means no matching record exists; it does not mean records were removed.

docs.title: Vehicles used
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle references with usage range and odometer values.

Only vehicles reported by this C file are listed. A vehicle-record link is offered only for an unambiguous master-data match.

docs.title: Positions
docs.text:
Figure: PLACE and GNSS records with nation, region and coordinates.

Open position map displays visible coordinates. Nation and region are shown as readable text plus technical value where possible. See Position maps.

docs.title: Violations
docs.text:
Figure: Reproducible technical pre-check for the selected C file.

The list explains rule, article, actual/target value, deviation and legal basis. It does not replace legal assessment of national exemptions, AETR or Article 12 cases. Saving a snapshot requires archive.manage; export requires archive.export.

Select evaluation period and enabled rule modules and recalculate whenever context changes. Results identify ruleset/module version, assessment range, calculation basis and severity; optional BALM amounts are guidance, not a fine decision. Review coverage and notices before each finding. Cross-module findings are consolidated only for the same driver, period and fact pattern.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
Figure: Certificate chain and signed-EF results.

VALID confirms a verified chain and all present signatures. INVALID and UNVERIFIABLE quarantine the file; the unchanged archive object remains available for evidence-preserving export.

docs.title: Importing e-invoices and XRechnung
docs.text: The guided importer processes UBL Invoice, UBL Credit Note, CII and hybrid PDF with embedded invoice XML. It reads the file safely, validates its structure and runs the bundled KoSIT validator. Nothing is written to the ledger until Create foreign-invoice draft is selected.

docs.title: Read and validate the file
docs.text:
Open Fleet > Import XRechnung, select an XML or PDF, or drop it onto the foreign-invoice list. Each file enters a queue. Inspect determines syntax, profile, Customization ID, hashes and available components.

Invalid documents are rejected without creating a draft. The KoSIT report remains available in the session and can be exported. Warnings require a business review; the summary identifies validator version and error/warning counts.

docs.title: Verify invoice data
docs.text: Compare document number and type, document/delivery/due dates, buyer reference or cost centre, currency, payment terms, and net, VAT and gross totals with the original. Credit notes are detected as a separate document type. Unsupported currencies or inconsistent totals are rejected.

docs.title: Match the supplier
docs.text: FLEET Mira compares VAT, tax, endpoint and company identifiers plus name and address with supplier master data. Review score and reason, then accept the best suggestion or select another supplier. If none exists, create a supplier from invoice data and verify it before continuing.

docs.title: Assign lines to vehicles and categories
docs.text: Every source line must be assigned completely to one or more vehicles and a cost category. ML suggestions are aids, not automatic booking decisions. Split line distributes a line to several vehicles or categories to the cent; Remove split removes the selected allocation. Source quantity, unit, net, VAT and gross remain traceable.

docs.title: Reconcile totals
docs.text: The tab compares invoice, source-line and allocation totals. Open net and gross must be zero for every line. Rounding differences, residual amounts or an unconfirmed supplier block creation of the draft.

docs.title: XML, PDF and validation report
docs.text: Invoice XML shows the structured source and KoSIT report the validation details. Hybrid PDF adds a PDF document tab. Preview uses an isolated temporary profile and never replaces the byte-identical original.

docs.title: Create the foreign-invoice draft
docs.text:
Choose Create foreign-invoice draft after validation, supplier, assignments and totals are complete. FLEET Mira atomically creates the draft, source lines and assignments and stores original, XML and validation report in the local financial archive. Failure leaves no partial invoice. An already imported source hash opens the existing invoice instead of creating a duplicate.

Open the resulting invoice tab, check its status bar, e-invoice data and originals, and complete the normal verification and booking workflow. Import requires finance.manage and the Pro E-invoice import feature; verification and booking additionally require finance.verify and finance.book.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: State Action KoSIT status rejected Open the report and request a corrected source document. Supplier is ambiguous Check identifiers in supplier master data or create a controlled record. Create action disabled Confirm the supplier and assign every line exactly. Totals differ Correct splits, VAT rates and rounding residuals. Hybrid PDF has no XML Request supported XML or a proper hybrid PDF.

docs.title: Foreign invoices
docs.text: Double-click a foreign invoice to open its own work tab. The status strip shows workflow, validity, local document and export states plus net/gross total, allocated amount and difference. Green means an exact cent-level match; red blocks verification.

docs.title: Header and supplier
docs.text:
Under Fleet > Foreign invoices > New, enter supplier, document type, invoice kind, number and date, delivery/validity period and payment terms. In the manual tax table, enter the taxable base for every VAT rate; FLEET Mira calculates read-only net, VAT and gross totals with commercial cent rounding. A 19% row is preselected and additional rates including 0% are supported. A credit or cancellation also references its original invoice.

The Supplier tab shows master data and e-invoice identifiers used for the document. Document data also shows dates, the VAT rate or complete tax breakdown, and net, VAT and gross totals.

docs.title: Positions
docs.text:
Every position belongs to one vehicle and category. Document date, valid from/to and Variable are inherited and locked. Costs increase and credits reduce the allocated amount. All positions must match invoice gross exactly.

For collective invoices, Split position distributes one source amount across any number of vehicles and allocates a possible VAT cent deterministically. A draft assignment is edited directly. After booking, Correct assignment creates a counter-entry on the wrong vehicle and a new posting on the correct one; already exported data receives a separate RECLASSIFICATION correction export.

docs.title: Original documents
docs.text: Add original document first writes the file atomically to the local financial archive, reads it back and verifies SHA-256. Locally verified enables verification, booking, preview and export. Back up documents now optionally replicates pending objects; failed external backup never blocks the business workflow. Preview uses a temporary copy.

docs.title: E-invoice
docs.text: For structured imports this tab shows syntax, profile, validator, errors/warnings and every source line with its allocation count. Original, XML and KoSIT report remain separate verified document roles. See Importing e-invoices and XRechnung.

docs.title: Document analysis
docs.text: Image PDFs and scans are analysed locally first using embedded text or Tesseract OCR. Rules and confirmed historical assignments provide review-only supplier, vehicle and lease-contract suggestions. Cloud analysis through an Azure or Vertex provider configured under Administration > AI connector requires explicit consent for each document. The original, hash, result, model, confidence and evidence remain traceable together; no assignment is confirmed automatically.

docs.title: Verify, book and correct
docs.text:
1. Complete header and positions in Draft.
  2. Ensure the required original is locally verified.
  3. Bring the difference to 0.00 and Verify.
  4. Use finance.book to Book immutably.
  5. Optionally export through accounting REST or CSV/ZIP.

Booked records are never overwritten or deleted. Cancel creates a counter-entry with a mandatory reason; a linked credit represents a commercial correction. Both preserve origin and use the correct sign in analysis.

docs.title: Export history and audit
docs.text:
Only booked or cancelled invoices may be exported. Idempotency keys prevent duplicates; external ID, timestamp and error remain visible for retries.

Creation, edits, verification, booking, cancellation, document verification and export are recorded. Navigation and preview create no event. Reading requires finance.read, editing finance.manage, verification finance.verify, booking finance.book, and export finance.export; Pro adapters also require their licence feature.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: State Action Verify disabled Check local document state and difference; e-invoice lines must be assigned completely. Difference red Correct position amounts, signs and rounding residuals. Document backup failed The local original remains usable; fix the target and retry backup. Booked invoice locked Create a cancellation or linked credit instead of overwriting it.

docs.title: Lease contracts
docs.text: Lease management combines contract terms, pre-calculation, payment schedule, vehicle documents and actual costs from supplier invoices. Contract management is available in every edition; reports in the Report dashboard follow its existing Pro and Enterprise licence boundary.

docs.title: Creating and opening a contract
docs.text:
Open Fleet → Lease contracts. Filter the list by contract number, vehicle, supplier and status. Hovering over a contract row shows a tooltip summarising contract number, vehicle, supplier, period, term, net rate, actual factor, annual and contract mileage, and status. New creates a draft; double-click opens the dedicated Lease: contract number work tab. A vehicle record contains Lease immediately after Foreign invoices and uses the same contract tooltip. All vehicle tachograph pages are collected below Tachodata.

One contract belongs to exactly one vehicle and one supplier. It records contract number and type, dates and term, payment timing, list and acquisition values, special and final payments, residual value, mileage terms, termination details and notes. Vehicle, supplier, contract number, start, end, term, net list price and actual net lease rate are mandatory fields marked with *; list price and rate must be greater than zero even for a draft. Components distinguish recurring services from one-time charges and identify mandatory amounts included in the effective factor. Activation establishes the binding status; ended and terminated contracts are immutable.

For a new contract, vehicle and supplier initially remain empty and must be selected deliberately. Contract date and handover date default to the current date. Contract start follows the contract date; contract end and planned return are calculated from contract start and term. The first due date equals contract start. The actual return date remains empty until the vehicle is returned. Changing contract date, start or term immediately updates the dependent dates.

The vehicle selector filters as the user types by vehicle number, registration and VIN. The supplier selector searches supplier number, name and creditor number. Search input does not need to reproduce case, spaces or separators exactly; only an explicitly selected result is stored.

docs.title: Creating a contract from documents
docs.text:
In addition to New, Pro and Enterprise provide From document. Document-assisted entry is a modal, transient session that can combine a contract, recurring invoice, standalone XRechnung, hybrid PDF and supplementary image documents. Originals are archived immutably with SHA-256 during the session and are excluded from backup synchronisation. No resumable intake drafts appear in the lease overview.

While OCR or worker analysis is running, the document list, status, preview and Cancel remain available; contract fields and Save are disabled. PDF and image documents open by double-click or Open in the integrated preview after another hash verification. A dedicated column identifies XRechnung documents and shows their validation status; Verify reruns KoSIT validation for the selected XML file or the embedded XML in a hybrid PDF. Analysis errors release the form for fully manual entry. Cancelling either the form or final confirmation warns before discarding everything. After confirmation, the session, analyses, reservations and local documents are removed; only the user, timestamp and discard event remain in the audit. Orphaned sessions without a heartbeat are discarded in the same way after 30 minutes.

Analysis uses valid structured XRechnung/ZUGFeRD data first, followed by embedded PDF text, local rules and OCR. Different normalised values are marked as conflicts. If a required field is missing, sources disagree or confidence is below 85 percent, the user can explicitly approve an analysis through the AI connector for each document. Azure and Vertex results only add suggestions and never silently replace a higher-priority source. Value, confidence, document and evidence location remain visible in the intake.

Suggestions populate the same lease form used for manual creation. Confident, uncertain and conflicting values are visually distinct, and every field remains editable. The review window separates conflicts, missing required values and all evidence locations. Open rows are entirely red and selected or completed rows are green; the field column sizes itself to its content. Dates, integers, currencies, percentages and tax summaries use the authenticated user's region and matching typed editors, while canonical storage remains ISO dates, cents and basis points. Conflict choices and completed required values are stored only in the active session, copied into the form and discarded completely if the intake is cancelled. Suppliers are matched primarily by VAT ID, endpoint or company identifier; vehicles by VIN and then registration. A unique result is preselected but still requires user confirmation. New: Vehicle and New: Supplier sit next to their respective selectors and open the existing prefilled master-data dialogs. Configured number sequences reserve an editable, deliberately non-reused number; without an active sequence, the number must be entered manually.

Before completion, FLEET Mira shows the contract, vehicle, supplier, period, recurring invoice, activation choice and posting mode again. All form values, new master data, contract activation and the default Post automatically mode require explicit confirmation. Contract, master data, verified recurring invoice, document links and monthly occurrences are then created in one transaction. A failure leaves no partial records, and the same completion request can be repeated idempotently. A contract without a recurring invoice remains a Draft by default. With a recurring invoice, activation and AUTO are preselected; if activation is cleared, the verified invoice remains assigned pending a later explicitly confirmed activation.

Figure: Contracts from the anonymised demo database with vehicle, supplier, term, rate and status.

Figure: Contract record with anonymised vehicle reference and M-data evidence.

docs.title: Leasing factor and actual rate
docs.text:
The pre-calculation follows the common vehicle-leasing comparison and is not a loan annuity:

Monthly rate = list price × leasing factor / 100

Leasing factor = monthly rate / list price × 100

The factor basis is explicitly net or gross. When a target factor is entered, FLEET Mira calculates the planned rate. If it is empty, the factor is calculated from the offer rate, or from the actual contract rate when no offer rate exists. The actual contract rate remains independently editable and is authoritative for the payment schedule and contract cost.

With net, rate and list price are compared before VAT; with gross, both include VAT. When both use the same tax rate, the factor remains practically unchanged apart from possible cent rounding because VAT cancels in the ratio. Differences can occur in particular when factor-relevant components use different tax rates. Difference from pre-calculation is the actual net contract rate minus the pre-calculated net planned rate; its percentage relates that difference to the planned rate. A positive value means that the actual rate is higher. The row appears only from an absolute difference of EUR 1.00; cent-only rounding differences are hidden. Special payments and components are excluded and instead appear in the effective factor and all-in monthly cost.

Every caption in the create/edit form and in the record tabs Contract and Calculation has a localized tooltip. In Calculation, the label and value expose the same detailed tooltip with the concrete numerical formula populated from the contract, its result, and its relevance to offer comparison, budgeting, contract control and variance analysis. Help text follows the authenticated user's language.

The actual factor compares the signed rate with list price. The effective factor spreads the special payment, final payment and mandatory factor-relevant one-time costs over the term. The all-in rate adds monthly service components and other one-time costs. This keeps offer comparison, signed terms and full cost transparent and separate.

Figure: Pre-calculation, actual contract rate, factors and full cost for the anonymised sample contract.

docs.title: Documents, invoices and mileage
docs.text: Documents links contract PDFs from the vehicle's document archive. Foreign invoices and Costs/Credits show actual postings linked at cost-position level; planned payments remain separate in the schedule.

docs.title: Recurring invoices and monthly posting
docs.text:
A verified supplier invoice of type Recurring invoice can be assigned from the contract's Recurring invoices tab. During the initial assignment, the user confirms the invoice, contract and posting mode. Post automatically is selected by default; Review manually presents each due period for approval instead.

The recurring invoice describes the repeating monthly supply. FLEET Mira creates stably identified occurrences with service month, due date, net, VAT and gross amounts. In automatic mode, the worker posts each complete, conflict-free due period exactly once. Overdue periods are caught up idempotently after a restart. An inactive contract, changed contract data, missing fields, total mismatch, duplicate period or unresolved variance moves the occurrence to Review required without a partial posting.

The posting mode can be changed with an effective date for future unposted periods. Posted months remain unchanged. The posting references the archived recurring invoice and service month; it does not invent monthly invoice numbers or record bank payments.

The payment schedule is versioned when a contract changes. Unchanged instalments retain their stable technical identity. In planned/actual reconciliation, zero cents is exact and up to one cent in each of net, VAT and gross is a documented rounding variance. Larger variances require a reason or correction.

Total mileage is proposed as an editable value using annual mileage × term in months / 12, commercially rounded to whole kilometres. An existing contract value is retained when the dialog opens. Changing annual mileage or term recalculates the proposal, which can then still be overwritten with a different contractual value.

The demo database contains six clearly marked fictitious contracts. Their monthly costs link to the existing leasing supplier invoices. Contract mileage is annualised from the first and last valid M_MIDNIGHT odometer readings in the evidence period and rounded to plausible 5,000-km steps. The evidence period and odometer readings remain visible in both the record and PDF.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
The Leasing group in the Report dashboard provides:

  • active lease contracts at an as-of date by vehicle;
  • active contracts ending in the selected date range;
  • active lease contracts at an as-of date by supplier.

All three reports start with vehicle number, registration and VIN and show contract rate, target, actual and effective factors, all-in rate and total contract cost.

docs.title: Driving-licence checks and RFID/NFC
docs.text: The driving-licence check links the recurring policy in a personnel record to an RFID/NFC identifier on the licence. A successful check automatically updates the next due date; the system-managed deadline cannot be completed manually.

docs.title: Requirements and master data
docs.text:
Open Fleet management > Personnel, select the person and choose Edit. Enter at least the personnel number and name and, where available, the licence number and issuing authority. Enable Recurring driving-licence check required and set an interval between 1 and 3,650 days; the usual initial value is 28 days.

The personnel record's Master data tab displays date of birth, licence data, the check policy and interval. Deadlines contains the automatically calculated due date.

docs.title: Assign RFID/NFC
docs.text:
1. Open the personnel record or Personnel > Licence-check evaluation and select the person.
  2. Choose Assign RFID/NFC.
  3. Place the chip on a PC/SC-compatible reader and verify UID, reader and person in the confirmation dialog.
  4. Save the assignment. A UID can be active for only one person; assigning a new UID ends the previous assignment with an audit trail.

The PC/SC UID is displayed and stored in the conventional byte order. For example, the byte-reversed sequence A3 BC 06 02 00 03 04 E0 returned by the reader appears as E0 04 03 00 02 06 BC A3.

Figure: Active and ended UID assignments with their validity period.

docs.title: Perform a PC/SC check
docs.text:
Open the personnel record or evaluation and choose Check via PC/SC. FLEET Mira accepts the check only when the UID read from the chip was actively assigned to the selected person at that time. Confirm the result. The record stores UTC time, method, workstation, result and operator.

A successful check completes the previous system deadline and calculates the next date from check time plus interval. No successful record is created for a missing reader, timeout, unknown UID or another person's UID.

docs.title: Evaluation and exceptions
docs.text:
Under Personnel > Licence-check evaluation, filter by person, state, check requirement, RFID assignment, email address and due-date range. The table shows the latest check, next deadline, remaining days and status. Its context menu opens the personnel record, assigns a UID or starts a check.

RFID CSV rows from a terminal are assigned automatically only when UID and timestamp match one active assignment. Unknown or temporally inconsistent UIDs appear in the RFID exceptions list. An authorised user may associate the row with a person or discard it with a mandatory reason; the source row remains traceable.

docs.title: Notifications, output and audit
docs.text:
Authorised users can preview or send a reminder from the evaluation. Print preview and PDF use the visible filters and columns. Changes to the policy, UID assignment, check, follow-up deadline and exception are recorded in object and global audit logs.

Viewing requires fleet.read; UID assignment, PC/SC checks and exceptions require fsk.check; manual notification requires fsk.notify.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: State Action No PC/SC reader Check the Windows driver and reader, reconnect it and reopen the operation. UID belongs to another person Do not record a check; verify the assignment and selected record. RFID missing Assign an active UID first. Deadline cannot be completed manually Record a successful check or disable the policy in master data. CSV row remains unresolved Check the timestamp and UID validity, then resolve the exception.

docs.title: Position maps
docs.text: Position maps display archived coordinates interactively. Viewing a map changes no business data and creates no audit event.

docs.title: Driver card
docs.text: Figure: C positions on OpenStreetMap with source and type filters.

docs.title: Vehicle unit
docs.text: Figure: M positions, border and loading records on OpenStreetMap.

docs.title: Operation and interpretation
docs.text:
• + / − zoom; drag to pan; All points restores the complete extent.
  • Source filters toggle PLACE, GNSS-3H and other records.
  • Type filters distinguish begin, RFU, three-hour GNSS, border and loading records where present.
  • Marker colours follow the legend. Click or hover to see time, source, type, driver/card or vehicle reference and available location text.
  • Filters affect display only; the archive object and position list remain unchanged.

The map uses OpenStreetMap tiles and displays the required attribution. Building the view requires connectivity to the configured tile endpoint; tiles may subsequently come from the local cache. A missing location name is not a missing point: coordinates can exist even when nation or region cannot be resolved unambiguously.

docs.title: Report dashboard
docs.text: The Report dashboard 💎 provides twelve reproducible working-time, mileage, return and deadline reports. Every run stores its filters, time basis, calculation version and result without changing tachograph, telematics or master data. The following screens and Stimulsoft outputs were generated from an anonymised copy of the demo database; activity times and evaluation results were retained.

docs.title: Catalogue and configuration
docs.text:
Figure: Report catalogue with groups, search, favourites, run history and output actions.

Use Configuration to maintain establishment/holiday country, optional subdivision, night-time window and return intervals. A stored report version retains the configuration in effect when it was created; later changes do not rewrite previous results.

Figure: Shared configuration for working-time and return reports.

docs.title: Driver working times by week
docs.text:
Purpose: Condenses daily working time, night work and total working time by ISO week. It supports checks of daily and weekly values and highlights unusual night-work shares.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Working times by driver
docs.text:
Purpose: Combines shifts, activities, countries, distance, day type and data quality for each driver. Use it for operational working-time review and investigation of individual days.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Monthly working times for all drivers
docs.text:
Purpose: Places all drivers in one matrix with daily and monthly totals. It makes workload, missing values and monthly differences easy to compare.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Working-time summary by country
docs.text:
Purpose: Assigns working time to countries or individual days. Rest and availability can be included for cross-border deployment and remuneration checks.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Mileage reports
docs.text:
The Mileage group contains reports by vehicle, by vehicle and month, by vehicle, month and day, and the Odometer readings per vehicle and day audit report. Filters select vehicles and a date range or from/to month. With no vehicle selected, all active vehicles are included.

Every new mileage and cost run uses the shared OdometerBoundaryResolver exclusively, with the priority M-file midnight → telematics sensor → C-file vehicle use → C-file place → C-file three-hour GNSS → telematics GPS. Only VALID and WARNING readings are eligible. Manual, unverified, unknown and conflicting values are excluded. Opening and closing readings are rounded to whole kilometres first; the displayed difference is then always exactly closing minus opening.

Qualified GPS-server values are stored as daily odometer readings independently of the 28-day position-detail retention. If a closed period is missing a boundary, administrators can use Administration → Cost analysis → Calculation parameters → Odometer determination to mark it incomplete, interpolate linearly or extrapolate. The default extrapolation is limited to seven days and uses the median of plausible daily distances from 14 days. Estimated opening, closing and difference values carry a warning marker. During the current local day, an available qualified actual reading wins. If none exists and extrapolation is configured, the central resolver estimates up to the current calculation instant. Monthly, overall and cost reports use the same closing boundary. If the opening boundary has no sufficiently recent reading, the central resolver applies the same minimum sample count, estimation basis and maximum gap: it derives the median from the first qualified following days and projects backwards from the first actual reading to the opening boundary.

Monthly and daily reports compare mileage with the immediately preceding calendar month or day for the same vehicle. Red and orange arrows indicate increases, blue marks the neutral range from −5 to +5 per cent, and light-green or green arrows indicate decreases.

docs.title: Odometer readings per vehicle and day
docs.text:
This report is the detailed audit trail for the other mileage reports and for cost per kilometre. The on-screen view uses a parent/child presentation: each vehicle is a coloured, expandable and collapsible group header. Internal number, registration, VIN, opening reading, closing reading and difference occupy separate sortable columns. The subordinate daily rows use separate columns for date, odometer reading and source or derivation (M file, C file, telematics sensor, telematics GPS, interpolated, extrapolated or incomplete).

For estimates, the tooltip provides the method, measurement time, supporting readings, estimate distance and algorithm version. The UI, Stimulsoft/PDF and Excel share the same vehicle groups; Excel merges the group header row. Runs above 20,000 daily detail rows are rejected and require a shorter period or fewer vehicles. Existing stored report runs are not modified by the new odometer-boundary-v2 algorithm version.

docs.title: Driver return to home/base
docs.text:
Purpose: Shows the last detected and next due return for selected drivers. Dispatchers and compliance staff can identify open planning needs before the deadline.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Vehicle return to the Member State of establishment
docs.text:
Purpose: Shows each vehicle's last return, return interval and next date. It supports fleet planning and evidence of regular return.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Personnel deadlines
docs.text:
Purpose: Combines personnel number, driver, due type, due date, remaining days, lead time, status and notes. It is the working list for driver cards, driving licences and other personnel evidence.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Fleet deadlines
docs.text:
Purpose: Combines time-based, mileage-based and earliest-of-both deadlines with current mileage, trigger, data quality and evaluability. It shows which vehicles require action because of date or mileage.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Leasing reports
docs.text: Active lease contracts by vehicle and Active lease contracts by supplier use an as-of date. Lease contracts ending soon uses a freely selected contract-end range. An optional supplier filter narrows all three reports. The result includes vehicle identity, contract, supplier, term and remaining days, contract mileage, actual rate, target, actual and effective factors, all-in rate and total contract cost.

docs.title: Create and output a report
docs.text:
Print layouts are tailored to the report's purpose: driver working-time and planning detail tables omit the Data quality column, while the driver working-time report prints each date completely on one line. The vehicle/day mileage report structures details hierarchically by Vehicle and Month; the daily odometer audit report visually separates Odometer from Source / derivation while retaining a continuous row background. Leasing lists use two-line records for contract/supplier and registration/VIN information, and the supplier report additionally groups by supplier. The violation dashboard prints Duration / deviation as a compact two-line heading.

  1. Open Fleet → Report dashboard 💎.
  2. Select Favourites, Working time, Mileage, Leasing, Planning or Deadlines, then choose a report.
  3. Set the report-specific filters that appear. No object selection means all permitted drivers or vehicles.
  4. Choose Create report.
  5. Open the run in Stimulsoft preview or export PDF or Excel.

The result view explains the calculation and time basis. Every master-data-related grid starts consistently with Vehicle no., Registration and VIN, or Personnel no. and Personnel name (last name, first name). Mixed deadline grids expose all five columns and leave non-applicable values empty. Global search covers every visible column, while headers sort by canonical raw values. Historic runs are normalized for presentation only; a personnel number that was not stored at the time remains empty. The stored source data is unchanged.

The 20 bundled Stimulsoft system reports use the same identity columns. Custom templates are not overwritten and receive the new canonical fields in addition to the existing compatibility fields.

Deadline reports can be filtered by period, object, due type, status and lifecycle. The fleet report additionally filters by basis, trigger, mileage data quality and evaluability. The deadline-specific selectors use a space-saving two-column layout; the compact object list still supports selecting multiple drivers or vehicles. If the period is not enabled, mileage-only deadlines without a date remain included.

Working time includes driving and other work. Availability and rest are included only in reports that expose the respective filter. Night work is calculated against the configured window and the time zone stored with the run. Daylight-saving transitions do not alter elapsed activity durations.

Dashboard access, configuration changes, start, completion, cancellation, failure, opening a stored run and export are audited. Entry requires reporting.dashboard.read; output and configuration may be restricted separately.

docs.title: Personnel and fleet tachodata evaluations
docs.text: The two overview workspaces group archived tachograph files by person or vehicle. They are the entry point to single-file analysis and show known coverage gaps and the next download due date. All times are UTC.

docs.title: Personnel
docs.text:
Figure: Personnel overview with download due date and data coverage.

Each parent row shows driver, personnel number, file count, data and activity ranges, next download and gap status. Data from/to is the complete range declared by the file, while Activities from/to is the range actually covered by parsed activity records. Search covers person, card, filename and archive ID. Date, gap and file-status filters can be combined.

Figure: Expanded driver-card files and archive coverage gaps.

Tachograph files lists linked C files with card number, archive date, period, filename, size, task, status, archive ID and path. Archive coverage gaps lists uncovered intervals between known data ranges. No gap is invented before the first or after the last range unless a business target period exists.

docs.title: Fleet
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle overview by registration and internal number.

The fleet view works the same way, but assigns M files through the confirmed vehicle link or VIN. Its separate activity range is derived from the actual M-file activity changes. Generation, parser and signature state remain visible per file.

Figure: Expanded M file and calculated vehicle data coverage.

docs.title: Due date and operation
docs.text:
• Green: outside the individual lead time.
  • Orange: within the default ten-day lead time.
  • Red: download due date has passed.
  • A dash means that no effective, unambiguous download due date can be determined yet.

Double-click a file to open the central driver-card or vehicle-unit analysis in one reusable work tab. The context menu offers analysis, archive record, single/selection export and ID/path copy. Export requires archive.export; viewing requires archive.read. Column layout, sorting, filters and expansion state are stored per user.

docs.title: Traffic-offence management
docs.text: This module supports fleet managers with the administrative processing of German traffic offences. It does not replace legal or privacy advice and makes no automatic decision about guilt, liability or the driver.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
While the Traffic offences workspace is open, it refreshes the review inbox and case overview from the database every 15 seconds. Selection and scroll position are preserved, and newly added review items are announced in the action row. Refreshing stops completely when the tab is switched away from or closed. The UI never triggers its own IMAP poll; it only displays results already imported by the worker.

Authority documents are accepted by upload, a watched import folder or a dedicated IMAP mailbox. Original files and messages are retained unchanged with a SHA-256 checksum. Text PDFs are read locally; images and scans can be processed with a locally installed Tesseract service. When a document creates a new case, its document type and date, authority, reference, registration, offence time and location, vehicle and response deadline must all be confirmed regardless of document type. When a document is assigned to an existing case, the review shows only the assignment, the required document date and the optional response deadline; the other case fields are hidden and are not requested again.

Once confirmed, the review-inbox item is immutable. View or a double-click opens the already linked case and cannot create a second case or assign the original to another case.

New and unprocessed review-inbox entries are highlighted with red text. Confirmed, rejected or already case-linked entries use the normal text colour. When a row is selected, the shared blue-and-white selection appearance always takes precedence.

docs.title: Case workspace and workflow
docs.text:
Each case opens in its own workspace tab. A localised progress indicator covers Case reviewed, Identify driver, Request driver response, Prepare authority response, Record dispatch and Close case. It consists of six cells inside one surrounding frame: completed steps are green, the active step is red and pending steps are yellow. All six cells are green after the case has been closed. The current task and all available actions are derived centrally from the domain workflow state. Actions that are not yet allowed remain disabled. The workspace reads worker and IMAP results from the database every 15 seconds while preserving selection and scroll position.

Below Case: [case number] - [authority reference], the following actions are available according to status and permissions: Edit, Refresh driver evidence, Confirm driver, Send driver request, Create fillable driver PDF, Prepare authority response, Record dispatch, Add document, Close case and Cancel case. Case data shows the confirmed master data. Edit opens a modal dialog; authorised users can save changes only after entering a reason. Previous and new values are audited. Changing the vehicle or offence time recalculates driver evidence, while a changed response deadline updates the document-specific due item.

Driver identification shows candidates and evidence with source, priority, validity interval, confidence and conflict state. An active person must be explicitly confirmed. If the evidence chain from tachograph data, telematics, dispatch and the default driver yields no candidate, any active person can be assigned manually with a reason. An automatically identified driver can also be overridden by the person who actually drove; this likewise requires a reason. Manual and overriding decisions remain visible as separate evidence and are audited.

Driver communication contains versioned requests and their related responses. The confirmed driver, email address, SMTP configuration and HTTPS portal are checked before sending. Portal link, return reference and fillable PDF are prepared transactionally and sent asynchronously. The case changes to “Driver response pending” only after SMTP succeeds. Failures remain visible and are included in the daily fleet-manager report. An intentional resend creates a new version and return reference.

Portal, PDF and email responses remain bound to the person and communication that were actually addressed. Raw data and extracted proposals are never overwritten. Review stores a separate confirmed snapshot. Without a preselected default, the reviewer must choose Continue driver identification or Prepare authority response; even an affirmative response never causes an automatic transition.

Authority response creates a PDF only from facts that the reviewer explicitly selects from previously confirmed data. Creating the PDF is not dispatch. Record dispatch captures the answered authority document, channel, time, optional evidence and note. Only the due item for the selected document is completed; any other open document deadline remains open.

The Documents tab contains the unchanged source document and all later additions, such as an objection, legal-protection confirmation or completed witness questionnaire. Internal document types distinguish driver declaration form, authority response and dispatch evidence. Later files are archived with a checksum in the same case file and never replace or modify the source document.

The Emails tab combines inbound messages correlated through IMAP and recorded outbound email in one chronological timeline. Sender, recipient, subject, status and readable message text therefore remain directly traceable from the case.

Audit shows revision-safe changes and workflow decisions. A regular close is allowed only after an authority dispatch has been recorded and no unreviewed driver response or open document deadline remains. Closing with open items requires the dedicated traffic_offences.close_override permission and a reason; open due items are archived rather than incorrectly completed. Cancellation also requires a reason. Closed and cancelled cases are read-only and cannot be reopened in version 1.

Driver identification evaluates only time-overlapping evidence in this order: M data, telematics driver history, dispatch and the historical default driver. A card in the co-driver slot or an unconfirmed card-to-person link is not driver evidence. Every assignment requires confirmation; overriding the highest-ranked proposal requires a reason.

When creating a case, the offence time is entered through a date-time picker. It defaults to the current time, displays date and time according to the signed-in user's region, and stores the instant normalized to UTC together with its local time context.

When assigning a historical default driver, the validity start is selected from a calendar. The date picker defaults to the current date and displays it in the signed-in user's regional format.

Drivers may respond through an internal HTTPS form, a personalised fillable PDF or free-form email. Vehicle use, allegation statement, address, comment and attachments are stored separately and always require review. An address supplied for a case never changes personnel master data automatically.

docs.title: Deadlines and notifications
docs.text:
The dedicated Traffic-offence deadlines view is nested directly below Traffic offences in fleet navigation; the opened workspace tab uses the same title. It refreshes whenever it is opened and after an authority document is confirmed. It displays only time-based domain data such as authority, reference, case, vehicle, confirmed driver, workflow and document status, due date and remaining days. Odometer, odometer source, target or remaining kilometres and distance-based filters are not used in this view. The first visible deadline is selected as the current row on the initial load. Light status highlights use contrasting dark text, while the current row uses the same white-on-blue appearance as the personnel deadline evaluation. Selection and scroll position are retained across asynchronous reloads without taking input focus away from navigation or filters. Double-clicking opens the related case.

Every confirmed document with a deadline receives a separate managed due item. Changing the date updates that item; only the recorded reply for that document completes it. Cancelled documents and documents confirmed as having no deadline archive the item with a reason.

The daily fleet-manager report contains pending driver declarations, replies due today or soon, overdue cases and technical errors. Addresses, free text, offence details, document contents and attachments are never included in the report email. The optional 2x2 widget is added only from the widget catalogue and does not modify existing layouts.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: The driver portal must be published with HTTPS inside the intended LAN/VPN. Access tokens are stored only as hashes, exchanged once for a short-lived session and protected by CSRF validation. Pro uses SQLite and the in-process worker; Enterprise uses PostgreSQL and FleetMiraWorker exclusively.

docs.title: Demo data
docs.text: The distributed demo database contains no traffic-offence cases. If required, the optional idempotent seed python scripts/seed_traffic_offence_demo.py creates 20 penalty notices clearly marked as fictitious and not payable. Each generated case is assigned to an existing vehicle, includes a synthetic enforcement-camera image and is registered with a document reference and test deadline in both traffic-offence management and the document archive.

docs.title: Vehicle costs and credits
docs.text: Direct costs and credits are entered in the vehicle record. Foreign- and e-invoice lines use the same cost ledger but are edited through the invoice workflow. Only booked entries contribute to cost analysis, the TCO data basis and reports.

docs.title: Prepare categories and suppliers
docs.text: Under Finance > Cost categories, maintain a unique code, label and business classification. Leasing, insurance and tax are usually fixed costs; fuel, repairs and tolls are usually variable. Supplier master data is needed when a foreign document is associated with the entry.

docs.title: Enter a cost or credit
docs.text:
1. Open Fleet > Vehicles, the vehicle record and Costs/Credits.
  2. Choose New.
  3. Verify the vehicle and category and select Cost or Credit.
  4. Enter description, valid from/to, document date, net amount, VAT rate and optional notes.
  5. Select Variable to allocate the full amount to the document date. Clear it to distribute a fixed amount by day across its validity period.
  6. Save the draft.

Net and VAT are stored to the cent; gross is calculated. Zero-percent VAT is supported. Fixed costs require a complete, ordered validity period. Foreign-invoice lines inherit document and validity dates from the header and remain variable.

docs.title: Edit, verify and book
docs.text:
A direct Draft can be edited and given an original document. Verify checks mandatory fields, periods, amounts and document policy. Book then moves it into the immutable actual-cost ledger. Buttons are enabled according to state and permission.

Booked entries are never overwritten or deleted. Cancel creates a linked counter-entry and requires a reason. A commercial credit is entered as its own type and reduces cost. Original entry, correction and operator therefore remain traceable in the audit log.

docs.title: Effect in cost analysis
docs.text:
• Variable costs and credits are allocated completely to the document date.
  • Fixed costs are distributed by day across the validity period.
  • Invoice and credit signs affect totals, comparisons and cost/km.
  • A cancelled booking and its booked counter-entry net to zero while retaining the booking basis.
  • Draft and merely verified entries are excluded.

docs.title: Original documents and permissions
docs.text:
Add document writes the original to the local financial archive, reads it back and verifies its SHA-256. External backup is secondary and never blocks the business workflow. Paper scans additionally require an organisational replacement-scanning procedure.

Reading requires finance.read, editing finance.manage, verification finance.verify, and booking or cancellation finance.book.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Problem Correction Fixed cost is flagged Enter a complete, non-reversed validity period. Edit is disabled Only direct drafts are editable; open an invoice line through its invoice. Entry is absent from analysis Check Booked state, reporting period and filters. Wrong period Correct document date for variable cost or validity period for fixed cost.

docs.title: Vehicle-unit analysis
docs.text:
Vehicle-unit analysis uses one selected M file as its base. Drivers, slots and card sessions remain separate; C files supplement comparison only within proven card insertion periods.

This makes the single-file view archive-scoped. Vehicle record > Day/Week/Violations, by contrast, uses all valid M archives assigned to the VIN. Check the heading's record/archive context before comparing periods or totals.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Figure: Generation, signature, vehicle identity, data range and parser warnings.

Warnings identify optional or incomplete download sections. Missing second-by-second speed data, for example, does not change the preserved M file.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Figure: Insertion/withdrawal, slot, card, generation and name.

“No assigned driver card” means no usable active card-insertion interval was found for the slot and period. It does not merely mean that a C file is absent; timeline tooltips explain this distinction.

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle activity intervals with data availability.

Driver changes and team driving are separated by card, generation and slot. Parallel activities from two drivers are never collapsed into one driver row.

docs.title: Day chart
docs.text:
Figure: Driver groups, insertion period and activity tracks for one UTC day.

Navigation depends only on the date. Driver and card appear in group headings. Tooltips on unknown-card groups explain their evidence basis.

Date, arrows and Go to control the UTC day. Each driver group shows card insertion and an activity track; colour and label distinguish driving, work, availability and rest/break. Hover details identify start, end, duration, slot, card and C/M availability. Unknown-card intervals remain a separate visible group.

docs.title: Week chart
docs.text:
Figure: One ISO week with separate driver panels.

Each calendar week appears once. Multiple sessions for the same driver are combined in that weekly panel; driver changes and team drivers stay separate.

Use arrows to move between ISO weeks and review each day's coverage first. Weekly totals apply to the visible range and record/archive context. Missing data is neither rest nor zero activity.

docs.title: Events and faults
docs.text: Figure: Records with code, description, start, end and section.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Figure: Second-by-second speed or a documented empty state.
